artigo.texto: A Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM) e a Semtech Corporation (NASDAQ:SMTC) expandiram sua parceria de fabricação de longo prazo por meio de um novo acordo plurianual, projetado para aumentar a capacidade de produção de silício-germânio (SiGe) para produtos avançados de conectividade de data centers. Anunciado em 13 de outubro de 2026, o acordo fornecerá à Semtech capacidade de produção dedicada nas instalações de fabricação da Tower Semiconductor nos Estados Unidos, Israel e Japão. O acordo visa atender à crescente demanda por tecnologias de interconexão óptica e de cobre de alta velocidade utilizadas em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial e centros de dados. O acordo ampliado dá continuidade a uma parceria que já dura aproximadamente 20 anos e inclui planos para desenvolver futuras gerações de tecnologia de conectividade. Os detalhes financeiros do acordo não foram divulgados. Capacidade dedicada de SiGe em três regiões de fabricação Nos termos do acordo ampliado, a Semtech garantirá capacidade de fabricação dedicada de SiGe nas instalações da Tower Semiconductor em três países. A distribuição geográfica tem como objetivo melhorar a resiliência do fornecimento e proporcionar maior flexibilidade de fabricação à medida que a demanda por componentes avançados para centros de dados aumenta. A tecnologia de semicondutores SiGe é utilizada em aplicações de alta frequência que exigem alto desempenho de sinal e transmissão de dados eficiente. A Semtech utiliza os processos de fabricação SiGe da Tower para diversos produtos de seu portfólio de integridade de sinal, incluindo amplificadores de transimpedância, drivers de modulador, drivers de laser e equalizadores lineares. Esses componentes suportam comunicações de alta velocidade, processando, amplificando e mantendo os sinais elétricos usados em sistemas de interconexão óptica e de cobre. As empresas esperam que a capacidade de produção adicional ajude a Semtech a atender às futuras necessidades dos clientes, ao mesmo tempo que apoia o desenvolvimento de redes de data centers cada vez mais avançadas. Ao garantir recursos de produção em várias regiões, a Semtech também visa reduzir sua dependência de locais de fabricação individuais. Acordo prevê suporte para conectividade de 800G, 1.6T e futura de 3.2T A expansão da produção abrange várias gerações de tecnologia de interconexão de alta velocidade. As empresas afirmaram que o acordo dará suporte aos produtos de conectividade atuais de 800G e 1,6T, bem como às futuras tecnologias que operam em velocidades de 3,2T e superiores. Esses avanços estão se tornando cada vez mais importantes à medida que as cargas de trabalho de inteligência artificial criam uma demanda maior por conexões de alta largura de banda entre sistemas de computação. Os modernos centros de dados de IA exigem que grandes volumes de informações se movam entre processadores, servidores e equipamentos de rede. À medida que a infraestrutura de computação se expande, o desempenho das interconexões pode influenciar a eficiência geral do sistema e a capacidade de suportar cargas de trabalho cada vez mais complexas. Os produtos de conectividade óptica e de cobre da Semtech são projetados para atender a esses requisitos por meio de processamento e transmissão de sinal de alta velocidade. O acordo de fabricação ampliado tem como objetivo fornecer a capacidade de produção necessária para dar suporte às gerações sucessivas dessas tecnologias. A Semtech destaca a importância da conectividade com IA O presidente e diretor executivo da Semtech, Hong Hou, enfatizou a crescente importância da infraestrutura de conectividade no suporte a sistemas de inteligência artificial. “A conectividade tornou-se um fator crucial para determinar o alcance da escalabilidade dos sistemas de IA”, disse Hou. “Atender a essa demanda exige planejamento de capacidade a longo prazo e compromissos firmes com nossos parceiros de fabricação.” Seus comentários refletiram a crescente importância dos componentes semicondutores que possibilitam a comunicação entre os sistemas de centros de dados. Com o crescimento da infraestrutura de IA, os fabricantes buscam garantir que a disponibilidade de componentes de rede acompanhe a demanda por equipamentos de computação. A ampliação da parceria com a Tower tem como objetivo proporcionar à Semtech maior visibilidade sobre sua futura capacidade de produção. A Semtech recebe o Prêmio de Inovação em Tecnologia Óptica O anúncio surge na sequência do recente reconhecimento do trabalho da Semtech em conectividade óptica de alta velocidade. Na Conferência Europeia de Comunicação Óptica (ECOC) 2026, a Semtech recebeu um prêmio de Inovação em Componentes Ópticos por sua família de amplificadores de transimpedância de 224 Gbps por canal. Os produtos são projetados para óptica linear plugável e são fabricados utilizando a tecnologia de processo SiGe da Tower Semiconductor. Os amplificadores de transimpedância são componentes importantes em receptores ópticos, convertendo sinais de corrente elétrica gerados por fotodetectores em sinais de tensão que podem ser processados por outros sistemas eletrônicos. O prêmio destacou uma família de produtos desenvolvida por meio da relação de fabricação já estabelecida entre as empresas. Também demonstrou a aplicação da tecnologia SiGe da Tower em equipamentos de comunicação óptica de alta velocidade. As empresas pretendem consolidar essa colaboração no desenvolvimento de futuros produtos de interconexão para aplicações em centros de dados. artigo.texto: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink warned that a halt to data center construction could trigger an economic slowdown. "If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," Fink told CNBC Wednesday, after BlackRock reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings early Wednesday. BlackRock advanced about 1% in late morning trading. "So much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex," Fink added, referring to the massive investments made to develop artificial intelligence infrastructure. Fink's warning comes as strong, local opposition to data center construction has emerged as a key issue in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, as communities struggle with rising utility costs, water use, environmental damage and questions over investment transparency. While Fink acknowledged fears about the data center buildout, he also noted "most of it is on misinformation." The stakes are high. Wall Street analysts estimate total AI capital expenditures could climb above $1 trillion in 2027 and total in excess of $5 trillion by 2030. "Data centers are not the problem. They're creating more new jobs than ever before," the BlackRock CEO explained. The scale of investment has created demand for construction workers, physical digital infrastructure, AI compute hardware and energy infrastructure to secure grid power, he said.

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no Dell despenca 11% e lidera queda de empresas de data centers por temor com IA Publicado 14/10/2026 • 18:07 | Atualizado há 13 horas OpenAI é processada em oito estados nos EUA devido a preocupações com a segurança do ChatGPT Bank of America contratou 1.000 terceirizados para corrigir falhas de software expostas pelo Mythos da Anthropic Trump vai recorrer da decisão que impede a Casa Branca de banir a MS NOW, a CNN e a Politico Netflix demite mais de 1.000 funcionários, cerca de 6% de seu quadro, em meio à desaceleração do crescimento ASML divulga resultados acima da expectativa do mercado, carteira de pedidos até 2030 e ações puxam índices europeus KEY POINTS Foto: Wikimedia Commons As ações da Dell despencaram 11% nesta quarta-feira (14) e arrastaram outros fabricantes de equipamentos para data centers, em meio ao aumento das preocupações de que os gastos corporativos com inteligência artificial não justifiquem a expansão da infraestrutura de IA. Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Oracle e Super Micro também acompanharam o movimento de queda. Leia também: Dell dispara 11% em NY após reportar faturamento recorde impulsionado por IA Em relatório enviado a clientes nesta quarta-feira, analistas do Barclays rebaixaram as recomendações para Dell, HPE e NetApp, após uma valorização significativa das ações e diante de dúvidas sobre o momento da adoção da IA pelas empresas. Os fabricantes de servidores para data centers e de outros equipamentos de infraestrutura estiveram entre os preferidos de Wall Street neste ano, graças ao otimismo de que venderiam grandes volumes de produtos associados à demanda por chips e sistemas de IA nos próximos anos. A Dell acumula alta superior a 300% em 2026, enquanto a HPE avançou cerca de 160% e a NetApp dobrou de valor. O sentimento em relação à infraestrutura de IA, porém, mudou recentemente, em parte por causa de dados preocupantes sobre a receita da OpenAI e do receio de que a alta dos juros torne mais difícil financiar uma expansão que depende fortemente de dívida. Leia também: Ações de Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave e outras empresas de IA despencam após dados sobre receita da OpenAI A Oracle, que recorre intensamente a empréstimos, caiu 9% nesta quarta-feira e acumula perda de 33% no ano. Já a CoreWeave, fornecedora de infraestrutura de nuvem para IA, despencou 15%, apagando seus ganhos de 2026. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC Os analistas do Barclays afirmaram que ainda não observaram uma “inflexão significativa da IA” nos gastos corporativos com produtos da Dell, HPE e NetApp. Por isso, reduziram a classificação das três empresas do equivalente a compra para manutenção. Na avaliação do banco, o aumento das receitas está relacionado à escassez global de memória, já que as empresas de infraestrutura repassaram aos clientes os preços mais altos desses componentes. Leia também: Wall Street avalia impacto de possível desaceleração da IA na expansão de data centers “Há um sentimento crescente de que a adoção da IA pelas empresas está criando uma renovação do parque de hardware”, escreveram os analistas do Barclays, acrescentando que as companhias costumam destinar apenas 5% de seus orçamentos de tecnologia da informação à IA. “Acreditamos que as fortes receitas corporativas sejam mais uma consequência dos custos de memória do que de uma migração para a IA empresarial neste momento.” Os analistas também constataram que apenas cerca de um quarto dos gastos corporativos totais com IA é destinado a hardware. Eles afirmaram que a normalização e, posteriormente, a queda dos preços de memória poderão pressionar as receitas das empresas de infraestrutura. O setor de memória é conhecido por seus ciclos acentuados, e as ações foram atingidas nesta semana depois que a chinesa ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) informou, no fim de semana, avanços em uma nova estrutura de chips. artigo.texto: The BYD Atto 8, known domestically as the BYD Tang L, became the brand’s first model with flash charging in Europe. It made an official debut at the Paris Auto Show 2026 with seven seats, a peak power of 764 hp, and a 136-liter frunk with a double-tap opening function. BYD executive vice president Stella Li presented the car. The BYD Atto 8 boasts the second-generation LFP Blade Battery from BYD. It offers a capacity of 115 kWh, suitable for 653 km of range under WLTP conditions. The biggest highlight of this pack is the flash charging function. It allows charging from 10% to 97% in nine minutes. The charging time from 10% to 70% is five minutes. The charging time increases by 3 minutes at minus 30 degrees Celsius. BYD plans to establish 6,000 flash chargers in foreign countries by the end of 2027. According to BYD officials, the Atto 8 is the most powerful 7-seat SUV in Europe. It offers a combined peak power output of 570 kW (764 hp, 775 ps). As a result, this model accelerates to 100 km/h in 4.6 seconds. The top speed reaches 240 km/h. The Atto 8 might be the most powerful seven-seater, but not the fastest. For example, the Audi SQ7 speeds up to 100 km/h in 4.1 seconds. The BYD Atto 8 is a large crossover with dimensions of 5040/1996/1760 mm and a wheelbase of 2,950 mm. Despite being available with five seats only domestically, this EV will offer three rows of seats in Europe with a 2+3+2 layout. The BYD Atto 8 has a 136-liter frunk that could be opened by double-tap. Another highlight is a projection-activated power tailgate. The BYD Atto 8 will start sales in Europe in Q1 2027. The price tag of this car has yet to be revealed. For clarity, the brand’s current seven-seater for Europe, the Tang EV, costs 75,000 EUR (83,885 USD) in Germany. However, according to the brand’s official website, the Tang’s price was reduced to 47,990 EUR (53,675 USD). The BYD Tang L EV (Atto 8 EV) costs 222,800 – 272,800 yuan (33,290 – 40,765 USD) domestically. According to China EV DataTracker, BYD handed over just 4,426 units of this model to owners in China from January to August 2026, down 87.5% Year-Over-Year.

artigo.texto: Mecklenburg County supervisors voted unanimously Tuesday to postpone until November any decision on a siting agreement for a proposed 100-megawatt battery energy storage facility northwest of Chase City. In another land-use matter, supervisors gave the green light for a proposed residential development in the Clarksville area, The Faireborough at Shiney Rock, which is described by its developers as a “Shire-like” village of 20 cottages on a family farm. In the Chase City area, TerraForm Power is proposing to build the Mitchell Energy Center on a 170-acre site near Fort Mitchell Road, Lenhart Road and Virginia 49, close to the existing Otter Creek Solar development. TerraForm Power says the battery facility would occupy about 10 to 15 acres, with the remainder of the site timbered. Access would be gained from Lenhart Road. Under an agreement being negotiated, TerraForm will pay the county $2.9 million after receiving a special exception permit authorizing the project to move forward. That payment would be followed by another $3.9 million over the project’s anticipated 20-year lifespan. Three Chase City residents — Kathy Keel, Charles Jackson and Carlos Davis — urged supervisors to reject the project. Davis, at times raising his voice, said battery storage, data centers and solar projects approved near Chase City “do nothing for us [the residents of Chase City].” He said he was tired of the town “looking like a dump site” because of the industrial development around it and would rather see more stores and amenities. Keel questioned whether the project could strain water resources needed by the town and raised concerns about possible contamination of nearby land in the event of a fire or other hazardous incident. Tony Deyerle, representing TerraForm, outlined what he described as the project’s economic and energy benefits. He estimated the facility would generate an $8.5 million economic benefit during construction, create as many as 30 jobs and produce another $6.8 million in tax revenue. Deyerle said the facility would help meet growing electricity demand, improve the resilience and reliability of the local power grid, and store energy for release when demand peaks. He also argued that the facility could help prevent future brownouts as Mecklenburg County’s energy needs increase. In the other land-use matter, supervisors approved Laurie Pearson’s request for a special exception permit to develop The Faireborough at Shiney Rock, a 20-cottage, “shire-like” village on a century-old family farm off Union Chapel Road. The owners have described the project as a woodland retreat of quaint, earth-sheltered cottages intended to attract tourism while preserving the area’s rural character. Tom Tanner moved to approve the permit. Tanner, Brenda Blackwell, Claudia Lundy, Board Chair Jim Jennings, David Brankley, Sterling Wilkinson and Dennis Spence voted in favor. Vice Chair Andy Hargrove and Kirk Gravitt voted against the request without explaining their votes. Nearby resident Herbert Ramsey and Clarksville resident David Billings opposed the project, questioning whether it was suitable for an area dominated by farmland. Ramsey told supervisors that he operates a trucking and hauling business nearby and that his property is zoned commercial rather than agricultural. Pat Charles, executive director of the Clarksville Lake Country Chamber of Commerce and a board member of Historic Downtown Clarksville, supported the proposal, saying it advances one of the county and region’s key goals: promoting tourism. In approving the permit, supervisors overruled the Mecklenburg County Planning Commission, which recommended denial of the project. In other business, supervisors also adopted amendments to the county zoning ordinance. The revisions grew out of an Aug. 17 review by the board’s legislative committee and a subsequent recommendation from the planning commission. County officials said the changes are intended to clarify and improve development standards. One amendment clarifies what vehicles and business equipment may be kept at a residence by someone operating a home-based business. Tanner raised the issue, saying the ordinance should not prevent lawn-maintenance operators from storing trailers, tractors or similar equipment at home. For lakefront lots, revised language allows certain accessory buildings to be placed toward the road-facing front of a parcel instead of beside or behind the house, helping homeowners preserve lake views. The amendments also clarify which large recreational equipment must be kept under cover. Other changes set a five-story height limit in R-3 residential districts to better fit the county’s rural character; adjust setbacks for accessory structures; extend the validity of a variance from one year to two; require food trucks to obtain permits from both the health department and fire marshal; clarify special-event requirements; require temporary construction facilities to comply with the Statewide Fire Prevention Code; and make a perimeter access road a condition of special exception approval for battery-storage sites. In other action, supervisors approved a boundary adjustment with the Town of South Hill and conveyed a 0.386-acre strip of land along Virginia 92 to VDOT to allow construction of a turn lane near Chase City.

artigo.texto: Microsoft Pushes Custom AI Chips with Azure Maia 300 Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation AI chip, as Maia 200 goes live, powering Copilot. Microsoft on Monday (Oct. 12) unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI accelerator, and said that Maia 200 is now in production, powering Copilot and other Microsoft cloud services. The company said it plans to scale deployments of its Azure Maia processor family at multi-gigawatt scale in 2027, positioning Maia as a primary inference system for Microsoft products and services, according to a blog post by Scott Guthrie, Microsoft’s executive vice president, cloud + AI. Microsoft said Maia 200 is deployed across its data centers in the US, Europe, and Australia, delivers up to 1.7 times more tokens per watt than leading GPU infrastructure, and powers built-in AI capabilities in Microsoft Teams, Copilot, and Cowork. By the end of the year, the chip is also expected to power GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry, a platform for developing, deploying, and managing AI applications and agents, according to Guthrie’s blog post. Maia 300, which Microsoft said will be deployed in production in 2027, is designed with an inference-first architecture optimized “for long-context, memory-intensive, and decode-heavy AI workloads,” according to the blog post. The company said the chip is expected to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems and, in a full 96-accelerator rack, up to seven times the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200. Like other hyperscalers, Microsoft continues to rely heavily on Nvidia and AMD GPUs for AI workloads. At the same time, it has spent the last few years building its own custom silicon to improve performance and efficiency across its infrastructure and cloud services. Unlike Amazon Web Services, which offers Trainium and Inferentia chips via public cloud instances, and Google Cloud, which provides access to its TPUs, Microsoft has not made Maia available to customer workloads via Azure instances. In Monday’s blog post, the company did not say whether that could change in the future. Because Microsoft is using Maia primarily for internal workloads, the competitive dynamic is different from a traditional chip war among hyperscalers, said Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. This is about Microsoft and other cloud providers delivering services faster, more efficiently, and more reliably. “That’s good for the customer because they’re getting better quality of service, and it’s good for the cloud provider because they’re doing it at lower cost, which means they’re more profitable,” Kimball said. Kimball said that Maia 300 appears to represent a significant step forward in Microsoft’s custom silicon strategy. “Maia 100 was a proof of concept. Then 200 came out, and they solved the issues they had seen in the 100. They are powering GitHub and Copilot,” he said. “It validated the design choices they were making, and 300 was where they said, ‘Let’s go big,’ and that’s what you are seeing with the Maia 300.” Microsoft’s plan to deploy the Azure Maia family at multi-gigawatt scale suggests broad global adoption across its infrastructure, Kimball noted. “It’s going to be used very broadly to support their workloads across the globe,” he said.

artigo.texto: Damion Smy Toyota agrees to $750 million HiLux, Prado DPF class action settlement 9 Hours Ago Deputy News Editor The Peugeot RCZ Vision has been revealed at the 2026 Paris motor show, with the French brand saying the sleek electric coupe concept previews the look of its future models both inside and out, as well as groundbreaking technology including solid-state batteries. A follow-on from the original petrol-powered RCZ coupe, based on the Peugeot 308 hatch and sold in Australia between 2010 and 2015, the four-seat RCZ Vision concept wraps the brand's upcoming technologies in its 'Feline Future' design language. This includes advanced solid-state battery tech, which promises to be safer and cost less than conventional lithium-ion batteries, as well as being much faster to charge and offer between 20 and 50 per cent longer range per charge. While not confirmed as a production model, the RCZ Vision teams a 1000V electrical architecture with Peugeot's higher-density, space-saving solid-state battery tech. This enables a 500hp (373kW) power output, yet with low claimed energy consumption of just 11.5kWh/100km, with the automaker targeting a 600km WLTP range from a battery pack that's only 110mm thick. Developed with US battery firm Factorial Energy, with which Peugeot parent company Stellantis entered an agreement in 2021, the solid-state battery enables a claimed 10-80 per cent charge in as little as 10 minutes. Beyond its battery tech, the RCZ Vision shows off Peugeot's upcoming design principles, which include an aggressive, muscular stance and new three-claw headlights, also seen on the E-T16 concept revealed in Paris, as well as three-claw tail-lights and an active rear spoiler. Massive 21-inch front and 22-inch rear forged aluminium alloy wheels complement its aggressive haunches, including triangular details in a nod to the original RCZ, while another reference to the original is the double-bubble roof design, which sits above a transparent glass cockpit. The cabin includes the 'Hypersquare' steering wheel seen in the E-T16, along with the 2025 Polygon and the 2023 Inception concepts. The Hypersquare wheel has been confirmed as a feature on the production version of the next-generation 208 hatchback, which is expected to be revealed in 2027, with the 2008 small SUV expected to follow. The RCZ Vision features variable-ratio steer-by-wire steering, reducing driver hand movements at low speeds while adjusting for smoother steering at higher speeds. The RCZ Vision is also the first Peugeot to use brake-by-wire technology, which replaces the conventional hydraulic connection between the brake pedal and calipers with electronic controls. Peugeot says this brings more precise braking modulation and greater efficiency through improved integration of regenerative braking. The Hypersquare steering wheel is teamed with the latest version of Peugeot's i-Cockpit, featuring transparent micro-LED displays positioning configurable data directly in the driver's field of vision, as well as a floating central display angled towards the driver. The recycled-leather-trimmed seats are asymmetrical and offer additional support towards the centre of the vehicle, while the centre console features physical machined-aluminium controls arranged on a piece of frosted glass. Space efficiency measures include movable air vents, which can be stowed when not in use, while a Serica analogue clock forms part of the cabin design. Peugeot's multiple concepts at its home motor show come as the French brand receives greater attention from parent company Stellantis. Earlier this year, Peugeot was named as one of four priority brands by Stellantis, alongside Jeep, Ram and Fiat, ahead of other marques in its stable including Alfa Romeo, Chrysler and Citroën. This bodes well for its future in Australia, after local importer Inchcape, which also distributes brands including Subaru, Deepal and Foton here, announced it would hand back the local Peugeot distribution rights it has held since 2017. A new Australian importer is yet to be officially announced and nor has Stellantis resumed local Citroën distribution following Inchcape's decision to cease distributing the smaller French brand in 2024, ending 102 years of sales in Australia. artigo.texto: PHOENIX — Gov. Katie Hobbs and her Republican opponent, U.S. Rep. Andy Biggs, have one thing they can agree on: data centers. Both reject calls for a moratorium on new data centers proposed by Attorney General Kris Mayes, with Hobbs saying it’s not the right approach. "I think there are places where data centers make sense, and they're an important part of the high-tech economy that we're growing here,” she told reporters last month. Biggs agrees. After last week’s gubernatorial debate, he said local communities should have the final say. “There are many who don't want them at all, and others that are willing to investigate and are thinking about getting them,” he said. Do you have a concern in your community or a news tip? We want to hear from you! Connect with us: share@abc15.com He pointed to Marana’s decision to approve a data center after Tucson’s city council rejected a proposal for a Project Blue facility, saying “the company’s moving to Marana.” However, the Marana facility is one of up to three sites Project Blue’s developer, Beale Infrastructure, is working on. The company moved the proposed Tucson facility to just outside the city, in an unincorporated part of Pima County, after the city rejected the project. Biggs and Hobbs both say Arizona needs state standards for water and power use at data centers. “That data centers pay for themselves,” Hobbs said. “That they're not raising utility costs on Arizonans. That they're using water sustainably, and that they're addressing real and valid community concerns about data centers in neighborhoods.” She pushed for the repeal of state tax incentives for data centers – a tax break she voted for when she was a lawmaker in the state Senate. Hobbs negotiated a three-year moratorium on the incentives in this year’s budget with legislative Republicans. “We landed in a good place, and we can still have conversations about the water use, the energy use,” Hobbs said in July. Biggs, who voted against the incentives when he was in the Senate, said he wants to get rid of them permanently if elected governor. “Well, the first thing we're going to do is, we're not going to provide taxpayer subsidies or incentives for data centers to come in here,” he said. Biggs said he’s met with industry leaders and told them they don’t need the incentives. “I haven't had anybody say that they would leave without those incentives or with the constraints that I've proposed,” he said. Biggs has proposed developers pay for all the needed infrastructure and that data centers not “encroach on current and future natural growth of water and energy policy.” Hobbs, who has said she still supports a repeal of the tax breaks, said the current three-year freeze on new applications is an opportunity to craft a data-center policy. "I understand that many Arizonans are worried about data centers, and we want to make sure we're addressing those concerns in the right way,” she said. Meanwhile, Mayes is holding a town hall in Mesa on Oct. 14 to discuss her proposed statewide moratorium on new data centers. “We need a temporary ban,” she told reporters after last month's attorney general debate. “We need a pause so that we can get our hands around this situation.” Mayes said she’s working on a plan for a new approval process that would allow communities to vote on data center projects and create a commission to review proposed data centers like the Arizona Power Plant and Transmission Line Siting Committee does for energy projects.

artigo.texto: Data centers have emerged as a top political issue in the 2026 midterm elections, and one of the few to unite Democrats and Republicans. A recent poll from Quinnipiac found 73% of voters say they would oppose the building of an AI data center in their community, including 55% of Republicans, 85% of Democrats and 76% of Independents. Those numbers were echoed in a recent Vermont Public poll that found 64% would support a ban on large-scale data centers in that state. The thing is, there aren’t any large-scale AI data centers in Vermont — or anywhere else in New England — at least not yet. This region isn’t seeing the data center boom that’s created so much controversy in other parts of the U.S. The week of Oct. 19, 2026, the NENC stations will explore some of the reasons why not in a special series called Awaiting Data. The week-long series will consist of audio, digital and video stories on topics including: - Why large AI data centers aren't being built in New England, and how the region is preparing for a future where they do come to town - Skepticism of the tech industry that’s fueling some of the opposition in our region - New England’s tradition of local control, giving residents a forum and tools to fight data center development - How leaders in the region’s tech and robotics fields view the role of data centers in the growth of AI - How retrofits of existing data centers could bring more AI capability to New England Awaiting Data’s contributing stations are WBUR, NHPR, Connecticut Public, and NEPM.

artigo.texto: GreenYellow and Tilt Energy Partner to Deploy Battery Storage at Industrial Sites GreenYellow finances and operates the batteries, while Tilt Energy handles their dispatch and market valorisation. The two companies launch a behind-the-meter storage offer with no upfront investment for industrial and commercial sites. GreenYellow and Tilt Energy announce a partnership aimed at accelerating the deployment of Behind-the-Meter (BTM) electricity storage systems in the industrial and commercial sectors. According to the two companies, the offer is built on an integrated, contractually backed Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). Energy storage is drawing in other players across different segments, such as Trinasolar, which is unveiling 760 W solar modules and battery storage in Vietnam, or, on the gas side, Naftogaz and Siemens Energy, which are considering five compressor units for Ukrainian gas storage. GreenYellow describes itself as an industrial orchestrator of flexible electrification since 2007, and Tilt Energy as a specialist in valorising electrical flexibility. A split of roles between financing and dispatch GreenYellow designs, finances, builds, operates and maintains the energy storage infrastructure. Tilt Energy handles its real-time dispatch and valorises the flexibility on electricity markets. The two companies say this complementarity gives customers access to a solution combining infrastructure, financing and energy management. They state that the offer allows customers to benefit from storage flexibility with no upfront investment, no exposure to electricity market risk and with contractually guaranteed performance. Company GreenYellow: company profile Three obstacles identified by the partners According to GreenYellow and Tilt Energy, many companies remain held back despite growing interest in batteries. The partners cite three obstacles: the level of initial investment, the technical and operational complexity of projects, and uncertainty around flexibility revenues. In the proposed model, GreenYellow bears the investment and performance commitments are contractualised. Operation of the asset and valorisation of its flexibility are entrusted to specialists, and the customer receives a turnkey solution. The two companies specify that the offer goes beyond a simple "Battery-as-a-Service" formula, without the customer having to handle the complexities of financing, operation and valorisation. Storage integrated into flexible electrification GreenYellow places this offer within a broader vision of flexible electrification. The company says the aim is not only to install a battery but to integrate it into a package combining energy efficiency, electrification of uses, local renewable power generation and smart management. "Electricity storage should no longer be considered as a mere energy technology, but as a full-fledged industrial infrastructure," says Mathieu Cambet, Strategy Director at GreenYellow. He adds that companies need solutions that improve their efficiency and resilience without tying up more capital. The context described by the partners combines volatile electricity prices, growing electrification of uses and the development of renewable energy. - Gas44.1 % - Nuclear16.1 % - Coal15.7 % - Solar10.6 % - Wind8.3 % - Hydro3.5 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.4 %

artigo.texto: O país abriga 71% da capacidade em construção na região, impulsionado pela inteligência artificial e nuvem. A expansão exige engenharia avançada e forte uso de energia renovável, consolidando o Brasil no mercado digital. O Brasil se firmou como o maior mercado de infraestrutura digital da América Latina. De acordo com o relatório da JLL, o país concentra 71% da capacidade de data centers atualmente em construção na região. Além disso, abriga aproximadamente 48% da capacidade instalada que já está em operação. Esse crescimento é impulsionado pela rápida evolução da inteligência artificial, da computação em nuvem e da digitalização dos serviços. A mudança de hábitos de consumidores, empresas e governos aumentou drasticamente a quantidade de dados que precisam ser armazenados e processados com segurança. - O Brasil lidera a América Latina com 71% dos data centers em construção. - A inteligência artificial e a nuvem são os principais motores dessa expansão. - A energia renovável brasileira dá vantagem competitiva ao país. - Data centers são estruturas críticas que exigem funcionamento 24 horas por dia. - A integração entre engenharia e operação reduz riscos e custos dos projetos. Energia limpa fortalece a competitividade A matriz elétrica brasileira, rica em fontes renováveis como hidrelétrica, eólica e solar, é uma das grandes vantagens do país. Essa característica favorece a implantação de data centers que atendem às metas globais de redução de emissões de carbono. Os novos projetos vêm incorporando soluções de eficiência ambiental, sistemas avançados de refrigeração e redução do consumo de água. Há também uma busca ativa por certificações internacionais, como LEED e normas ISO, que garantem a sustentabilidade das operações. Apesar da energia limpa, o setor exige grandes volumes de energia com qualidade e estabilidade. Marco Alberto Silva, cofundador e CEO do Grupo Engemon, afirma que um data center precisa ser concebido como um ecossistema integrado. Sistemas elétricos, climatização, automação, conectividade, segurança e prevenção de incêndios devem funcionar de maneira coordenada, com alta disponibilidade e redundância. É essa visão completa que permite reduzir riscos e garantir a continuidade das operações. Engenharia integrada reduz riscos e prazos Os data centers são estruturas de missão crítica, onde uma interrupção pode comprometer serviços financeiros, bancos digitais e sistemas públicos. A Engemon atua nesse mercado oferecendo soluções que vão do planejamento à manutenção, acompanhando o empreendimento em todas as fases. A atuação integrada permite compatibilizar sistemas elétricos, mecânicos, de automação e segurança. Em uma instalação que funciona ininterruptamente, essa coordenação é essencial para a confiabilidade. Silva acrescenta que na Engemon, trabalhamos para que cada solução seja dimensionada de acordo com a realidade e as necessidades do cliente. A integração entre engenharia, construção, tecnologia, operação e manutenção permite antecipar interferências, acelerar a implantação e entregar uma infraestrutura mais segura, eficiente e preparada para futuras expansões. A empresa também integra serviços de operação e monitoramento contínuo. Esse modelo reduz a fragmentação entre fornecedores diferentes e aumenta a previsibilidade, essencial em projetos de alta complexidade técnica e grandes investimentos. Desafios para o protagonismo global Ainda que líder na região, o Brasil precisa expandir sua infraestrutura energética e fortalecer a conectividade para se aproximar dos maiores mercados globais. É necessário estimular a formação de profissionais especializados e oferecer previsibilidade regulatória para investimentos de longo prazo. A demanda deve continuar crescendo com a popularização da inteligência artificial generativa e a digitalização industrial. O relatório da JLL aponta que os mercados de colocation e hyperscale mantiveram crescimento sustentável na América Latina em 2025, com o inventário de colocation da região avançando 20% em um ano. Empresas que integram engenharia, tecnologia e sustentabilidade terão papel estratégico na transformação do potencial brasileiro em infraestrutura efetiva. O próximo passo é transformar as vantagens territoriais e energéticas em condições para que o país avance entre os principais polos globais da economia digital.

artigo.texto: - Ukrainian drones attacked Russia's largest data center, targeting Russia's AI ambitions. - Sberbank's systems remain operational; Yandex's supercomputers' status is unclear. - Western sanctions are also hindering Russia's AI progress, complicating its chip purchases from China. MOSCOW — Ukrainian drones hit Russia's biggest data center on Wednesday, part of a series of attacks appearing to target Moscow's ambitions to develop Russian artificial intelligence capabilities on a par with those from the U.S. and China. The strike on the Balakovo data center, owned by Sberbank, the country's largest bank and technology company, followed three attacks in the past week on data centres owned by Russian technology group Yandex. "We confirm that the data processing center was attacked. At the same time, all of Sberbank's systems and services are operating normally and without disruption," Sberbank First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin told reporters. President Vladimir Putin held a previously unannounced meeting on Wednesday with top officials on "information security," in which Sberbank CEO German Gref took part. The Kremlin said that the meeting was not linked to the attacks on data centers. Russia's state RIA Novosti news agency reported in 2024 that the Sberbank center hit on Wednesday would host Russia's biggest supercomputer, which is scheduled to go into operation in 2027. The Yandex data centres, hit earlier, hosted all three of that company's operating supercomputers. Neither Yandex nor Sberbank has said whether supercomputers, used to train the AI models, were damaged in the Ukrainian attacks. Along with Yandex, its main domestic rival, Sberbank is Russia's leading developer of artificial intelligence. The domestic market is shared between Sberbank's GigaChat model and YandexGPT. Difficulties purchasing chips Both companies have invested heavily in the development of their models but lag global leaders in the United States and China by up to nine months, according to Sberbank's own estimates, partly due to Western sanctions which hinder Russia's access to the most advanced hardware. "It's clear what difficulties we face when purchasing modern graphics processing units. Both we and Yandex suffer from this," Gref said on Sept. 29, calling it the biggest reason why Russia lags behind the U.S. and China in AI. Sberbank is in talks to buy chips from Chinese makers, but in an interview with Reuters on June 3, Vedyakhin said that chipmaker Nvidia's monopoly on its CUDA software platform, which has become an AI industry standard, is an even greater problem. Yandex said previously that its supercomputers operated on Nvidia A100 chips, a model launched in 2020 and since then succeeded by more advanced H100 chips. Sberbank has two functioning supercomputers. The most advanced one, called Christofari Neo, ranked 167th in the Top 500 list of the world's most powerful supercomputers, is located in Moscow and is based on Nvidia A100 chips. Yandex's most advanced Chervonenkis supercomputer is ranked No. 101 in the same list. IT expert Mikhail Klimarev told Reuters it could take a long time to replace the chips due to Western sanctions, while damage to the supercomputers could set back the Russian AI industry, which already suffered from sanctions. "The equipment is being imported, but it's done at a high cost, through indirect routes. First, you need to negotiate so that someone is willing to sell it to you and is not afraid of sanctions," he said. Protect assets Some commentators compared the lack of reported disruption at state-controlled Sberbank with Yandex, whose taxi and food delivery units had reported disruptions, saying it showed that Sberbank's centers are better protected. "This is a great example of what a business owner can do to protect their assets," wrote military blogger Alexander Kots. Under an August decree by Putin, the state can take over administration of poorly protected facilities. The Sberbank site is located close to the Balakovo nuclear power plant, which the data centre uses as an energy source, and the Saratov hydroelectric power plant. No damage was reported to either plant from the attack. Ukraine says it is responding to Russian attacks on its own data sites. Both countries have attacked each other's refineries, power stations, ports and e-commerce companies. Russia's digital development ministry said this week it was in talks with the military on protecting the data centers, while some lawmakers called for them to be moved underground where the hardware will be out of reach for drones. "We need a so-called Doomsday data vault," Valery Yermakov, deputy CEO of state-controlled Rostelecom, another major data center operator, told a conference in Moscow. Contributing: Gleb Stolyarov

artigo.texto: Maxxen Day 2026 welcomed energy industry executives, investors, project developers, technology companies and business partners from all across the European continent, from the UK to Türkiye. Maxxen Energy’s factory in Ayd?n, Türkiye, opened in December 2025. In just nine months, the company has delivered more than 600 MWh across 20+ projects, reaching nearly 5% of the European grid-scale BESS market. Maxxen believes this makes it the fastest-growing European BESS manufacturer ever. At the event, Maxxen also announced its membership of SolarPower Europe. The future of Europe’s energy storage market took centre stage Sessions explored the technology landscape, market dynamics and revenue outlook for Europe’s energy storage market. Panels looked at how to finance the investments needed to meet the growing demand for flexibility, and at the role of risk management and insurance in securing that financing. Project developers shared what they learned moving from their first projects to large-scale portfolios, and the challenges of scaling. Sessions and panels featuring international companies including Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, Wood Mackenzie, Clean Horizon, Solas Capital, Volteo Capital, Gresham House, Munich Re, Zagope, Luxera and Crowmie brought perspectives from across the BESS value chain. “We are shaping the future of the industry, together” Ruben Valiente, Managing Director of Maxxen Energy, said: “At Maxxen Day we opened our factory in Türkiye to the European battery storage industry and showed what we believe is one of the most advanced BESS factories in Europe. We also believe Maxxen is the fastest-growing European BESS manufacturer ever, with more than 600 MWh delivered in just nine months. It was a privilege to host guests from all across the European continent, from the UK to Türkiye. Many told us it was one of the best industry events they had attended. None of this happens without people and culture. My thanks go to the Maxxen Energy team, and to our colleagues in Türkiye in particular, who work tirelessly and welcome everyone with great warmth. As a European company, we are proud to contribute to Europe’s energy transition, and we look forward to doing so alongside our peers at SolarPower Europe.” Guests saw the factory in action After the sessions, the programme continued with factory tours and product presentations. Guests followed the production of battery energy storage systems step by step and spoke directly with Maxxen’s engineering and technical teams. A networking gathering gave participants time to continue the conversation and build new business connections. On the second day, guests took part in a cultural programme showcasing the heritage of the Aegean region.

artigo.texto: Microsoft purchases over 600 acres in Woodward to build a data center In a residents-only community meeting Monday night, Woodward’s mayor and Microsoft representatives unveiled plans for the company to build a data center within city limits. More than 200 residents gathered in the auditorium of Woodward-Granger High School to hear details about the project and express their opinions. It comes as Microsoft purchased over 600 acres of land in Woodward late last week. The land was purchased from an independent seller, not from the city. It’s already zoned for industrial use, which includes data centers. Tempers flared within the meeting, with one person being escorted out by police as Microsoft officials and Mayor Todd Folkerts answered questions about the project. Many said they were frustrated at the lack of community involvement in the project. “Is this something that we get a vote on? I mean, something this big, the community should get to vote on instead of doing back-ended deals,” one resident said. Folkerts said residents would not get to vote on the matter, but city council would vote on negotiations between Microsoft and the city. Microsoft representatives said the project would bring dozens of jobs, increase the tax base, and would not impact utility costs for residents. Something Folkerts says is necessary. “I can safely say I have not seen a single one of you at a budget meeting when we try to balance a budget for this community,” he said to the crowd. “We have to find revenue sources for our community.” But frustrations extended beyond the data center. The meeting, which replaced the city’s regular city council meeting, was open to Woodward residents only. Attendees had to show proof of residency to get inside, and several people were turned away. Randy Evans, president of Iowa’s Freedom of Information Council, was one of the people turned away. He said requiring proof of residency goes against Iowa’s open meeting laws. “It runs counter to the openness that the public meetings all guarantee,” Evans told KCCI. “From my vantage point, it erodes the trust and confidence, and the respect for Woodward city government.” Microsoft said the building has not been designed, and doing so would take roughly two years before construction could even begin.

artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no A vantagem brasileira na corrida pelos data centers Publicado 14/10/2026 • 12:00 | Atualizado há 12 horas OpenAI é processada em oito estados nos EUA devido a preocupações com a segurança do ChatGPT Bank of America contratou 1.000 terceirizados para corrigir falhas de software expostas pelo Mythos da Anthropic Trump vai recorrer da decisão que impede a Casa Branca de banir a MS NOW, a CNN e a Politico Netflix demite mais de 1.000 funcionários, cerca de 6% de seu quadro, em meio à desaceleração do crescimento ASML divulga resultados acima da expectativa do mercado, carteira de pedidos até 2030 e ações puxam índices europeus Foto: Divulgação/Ascenty A inteligência artificial parece existir na nuvem, mas sua infraestrutura é profundamente física. Por trás de cada modelo ou agente inteligente existem servidores, chips, redes, sistemas de refrigeração e instalações que funcionam 24 horas por dia. A nuvem, afinal, tem endereço, ocupa terreno, consome energia e precisa ser resfriada. Estamos entrando em uma transformação mais profunda: inteligência deixa de ser apenas uma capacidade humana e passa a existir também como infraestrutura disponível em escala. Carros poderão dirigir sem motorista, fábricas operar com crescente autonomia e agentes de IA comprar, contratar e negociar. Governos poderão antecipar congestionamentos, fraudes e falhas de infraestrutura. É a capacidade de produzir, decidir e antecipar multiplicada por milhões de máquinas. Mas inteligência em escala exige energia em escala. Segundo a Agência Internacional de Energia, os data centers consumiram cerca de 485 TWh de eletricidade em 2025 e poderão chegar a 950 TWh em 2030, ligeiramente mais que todo o consumo atual do Japão. A revolução aparentemente imaterial da IA encontrou um limite concreto: eletricidade. Isso começa a mudar a geografia da economia digital. Conectividade, segurança e talentos continuam importantes, mas uma nova pergunta entrou na mesa: onde está a energia? Servidores podem ser instalados rapidamente; redes de transmissão e geração levam anos. A infraestrutura digital começa a correr mais rápido do que a energética que precisa sustentá-la. Há ainda a água. Sistemas de refrigeração podem demandar volumes relevantes. A questão não é ser a favor ou contra data centers, mas quais queremos, onde instalá-los e com que padrões de eficiência. Reúso de água, refrigeração eficiente e energia de baixo carbono podem transformar restrição ambiental em vantagem competitiva. É aqui que o Brasil ganha relevância. Em 2025, 86,8% da matriz elétrica brasileira foi renovável; eólica e solar responderam juntas por 26,4% da geração. Poucos grandes mercados combinam escala territorial e econômica com uma matriz dessa natureza. Na economia da IA, um ativo que durante décadas enxergamos principalmente como ambiental passa a ser também tecnológico. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC A dimensão do movimento já aparece nos números. Em junho de 2026, o Ministério de Minas e Energia informou 38 GW em pedidos de acesso relacionados a data centers, dos quais 7,1 GW estavam associados a cerca de R$ 159 bilhões em investimentos previstos. Os 38 GW superam em mais de duas vezes e meia a capacidade instalada de Itaipu. São grandezas distintas, mas revelam a pressão potencial sobre o sistema. O Redata, aprovado pela Câmara em fevereiro, prevê benefícios tributários e contrapartidas. Mas a questão decisiva será menos quantos servidores atrairemos e mais quanto valor permanecerá no país. Um data center isolado é infraestrutura. Ligado a energia, telecomunicações, software, universidades, fornecedores e talentos, pode integrar um ecossistema de inovação. Estados e municípios disputarão esses investimentos como no passado disputaram montadoras e siderúrgicas. Os vencedores dificilmente serão os que oferecerem apenas o maior incentivo fiscal, mas os que conseguirem combinar energia, água, conectividade, licenciamento, qualificação profissional e integração com a economia regional. A próxima fronteira da inteligência artificial será definida tanto pelos algoritmos quanto pela infraestrutura capaz de executá-los. O Brasil pode transformar energia de baixo carbono, eficiência ambiental e escala territorial em uma razão para esses investimentos virem para cá. Na economia da IA, sustentabilidade não precisa ser o preço que se paga pelo desenvolvimento. Pode ser uma de suas vantagens competitivas. artigo.texto: Câmara aprova urgência para PL que muda divisão de custos de armazenamento de energia Em redação dada pela lei de 2025, foi fixado que os sistemas de armazenamento de energia, na forma de baterias, terão custos de contratação rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta terça-feira (13) o requerimento de urgência do projeto de lei que abre margem para o custo da contratação de baterias ser arcado pelos usuários finais de energia elétrica do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), incluídos os consumidores. Ainda não há data para a votação do mérito do texto (PL 3716/2026), que deve ficar para após o segundo turno. Em redação dada pela lei de 2025, foi fixado que os sistemas de armazenamento de energia, na forma de baterias, terão custos de contratação rateados apenas entre os geradores de energia. Isso gerou críticas do setor e um dos argumentos é a falta de um tratamento isonômico. As baterias serão contratadas na modalidade de "reserva de capacidade". Em geral, os custos administrativos e financeiros e os encargos tributários precisam ser rateados entre todos os usuários finais de energia elétrica do SIN, incluídos os consumidores. A exceção, contudo, foi dada aos sistemas de armazenamento de energia. A proposta de mudança é do deputado Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP). O tema é controverso porque a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) já está trabalhando na regulamentação do tema com base na legislação em vigor. Os inéditos leilões para baterias estão previstos para dezembro. Em nota conjunta, um grupo de seis entidades apontou que o armazenamento de energia, inclusive em baterias, é capaz de reduzir outros encargos suportados pelo consumidor ao otimizar a operação do parque gerador em suas diversas fontes. Foi citado estudo da Volt Robotics, ao demonstrar que as baterias podem reduzir a variação do preço da energia (PLD) e o acionamento de termelétricas, gerando economia superior a R$ 1,6 bilhão ao ano para o consumidor. "Os custos da reserva de capacidade são distribuídos entre todos os usuários finais, conforme parâmetros definidos em lei. Porém, apenas os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias são tratados de maneira diversa, sendo custeados exclusivamente pelos geradores e sem definição legal dos parâmetros de custeio", apontou o grupo de entidades. Assinaram a nota conjunta: a Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (ABEEólica), a Associação Brasileira dos Investidores em Autoprodução de Energia (Abiape), a Associação Brasileira da Indústria do Hidrogênio Verde (ABIHV), a Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE), a Associação Brasileira de Energia Solar Fotovoltaica (Absolar) e a Associação Brasileira dos Produtores Independentes de Energia Elétrica (Apine). O que diz a ABSAE? A Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (ABSAE) disse em nota que o avanço da proposta com urgência aprovada hoje "é importante para ampliar a segurança jurídica e criar condições mais previsíveis para a realização dos primeiros leilões de baterias em larga escala no Brasil". "A aprovação da urgência representa um avanço para que o Congresso discuta o tema com a celeridade necessária. Em paralelo precisamos olhar para o prazo dos leilões: o sistema elétrico necessita de potência adicional em 2028, e é plenamente possível corrigir a isonomia no rateio enquanto prossegue o cronograma. Assim vamos equilibrar segurança energética, redução de custos sistêmicos e segurança jurídica", afirma Fabio Lima, diretor-executivo da ABSAE.

artigo.texto: ACC (Automotive Cells Company) JV Stellantis, Mercedes, Saft Exide Technologies, headquartered in France, has introduced Solition Powerflex, a modular battery energy storage system (BESS) intended for commercial and industrial use, renewable energy integration, e-mobility infrastructure and agricultural facilities, ESS News reported. The product combines a 261 kWh LFP battery with a 125 kW bidirectional power conversion system (PCS) housed in an outdoor cabinet. In grid-connected setups, as many as 15 cabinets may be paralleled, delivering a maximum combined capacity of 3.915 MWh and 1.875 MW of power output. Off-grid installations can accommodate up to five cabinets. Within each cabinet sit five battery packs, each rated at 52.25 kWh and based on 314 Ah LFP cells. Charge and discharge rates reach 0.5C, while the system runs at 400 V AC and either 50 Hz or 60 Hz. Per the manufacturer's technical datasheet, nominal round-trip efficiency stands at 86%, inclusive of auxiliary power consumption. The IP55-rated outdoor cabinet has dimensions of 1,000 mm x 1,420 mm x 2,250 mm and a weight of approximately 2,720 kg, taking up roughly 1.42 m2. It is built to run at ambient temperatures from -20 C to 50 C, with power derating kicking in above 45 C. A dual-loop liquid cooling and heating system handles thermal management, using separate circuits for the battery and the power conversion system, rated at 5 kW and 3 kW respectively. Built into the cabinet are a battery management system, energy management system, PCS, thermal management and fire protection equipment. Safety provisions encompass automatic aerosol fire suppression, emergency shutdown, audible and visual alarms, explosion relief devices and a dedicated external firefighting interface. Exide stated that the system features a European-developed Storage Control System (SCS) that permits integration with on-site generation assets, grid operators and energy markets. Applications supported include peak shaving, self-consumption optimization, spot-market trading and ancillary services. The control platform further delivers remote monitoring, over-the-air software updates and interfaces for third-party systems. Exide noted that its digital architecture encompasses encrypted remote connections, EU-based data hosting and multilayer access controls. Serge Arbes, senior business director global, energy solutions, at Exide Technologies, said organizations increasingly want to boost energy resilience, integrate renewable generation and optimize energy costs. He added that Solition Powerflex was created to meet these evolving requirements, pairing a scalable architecture with advanced control capabilities in a solution able to adapt to shifting business needs. Standard warranty terms were not disclosed by Exide. The technical datasheet notes that battery capacity and system warranty conditions can be obtained upon request. artigo.texto: Cegonha com carros da BYD tomba em Recife (PE) e causa prejuízo milionário Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), o sinistro ocorreu por volta das 4h da madrugada no Km 52 da BR 101, em Paulista, sentido Abreu e Lima Uma carreta com onze carros modelo Dolphin GS, da BYD, tombou no início da manhã desta quarta-feira (14), em Paulista, na Região Metropolitana do Recife (PE). Segundo a Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), o sinistro ocorreu por volta das 4h da madrugada no Km 52 da BR 101, em Paulista, sentido Abreu e Lima. “A suspeita é de que o motorista de um caminhão cegonha perdeu o controle do veículo em uma curva e tombou”, afirmou a PRF. Segundo o órgão federal de fiscalização rodoviária, o motorista ficou ferido e foi encaminhado para uma unidade de saúde. O caminhão está tombado sobre o canteiro central. Cada unidade do BYD Dolphin GS é vendida por R$ 150 mil. Com isso, o prejuízo passa de R$ 1,5 milhão. Apesar do ocorrido, não houve registro de fogo após o acidente com os carros elétricos. Como é o BYD Dolphin GS? O Dolphin GS é o segundo carro elétrico mais vendido do Brasil. Com uma bateria de 44,9 kWh ele consegue rodar 291 km com uma carga completa, segundo os números do Inmetro. Na parte de desempenho, o Dolphin GS tem 95 cv de potência e 18,3 kgfm de torque. A aceleração de 0 a 100 km/h acontece em 10,9 segundos. O modelo vem equipado com chave presencial, piloto automático, sistema de monitoramento da pressão dos pneus, câmera 360º, comandos de voz, conexão de smartphone sem fio com a multimídia e mais. - Comprimento: 4,13 m; - Largura: 1,77 m; - Altura: 1,57 m; - Distância entre eixos: 2,70 m; - Distância do solo: 150 mm.

artigo.texto: O novo "reduto" da China em sua ambição de construir o maior centro de dados do mundo. A área parece uma miragem de alta tecnologia. Fileiras de enormes centros de dados, tanto recém-concluídos quanto em construção, erguem-se em meio a planícies onduladas e campos de girassóis e sorgo. Os edifícios ostentam os nomes de algumas das maiores empresas de tecnologia da China , desde a gigante de hardware Huawei e a plataforma de mídia social Kuaishou até a provedora de serviços VNET. Todas estão concentradas em uma área constantemente movimentada por atividades de construção e operação. Esta é Ulanqab, uma cidade na Região Autônoma da Mongólia Interior, na China, localizada na orla do Deserto de Gobi. Ela está se tornando rapidamente um dos polos de dados que impulsionam o poderoso boom da inteligência artificial (IA) na China, posicionando o país como o único rival verdadeiramente formidável dos EUA em sua ambição de domínio tecnológico. Quase 90 data centers estão planejados para serem construídos nesta cidade com menos de 2 milhões de habitantes. Ulanqab possui um número crescente de centros de dados de IA e big data, demonstrando as vantagens que a China está ganhando na corrida para desenvolver tecnologias que podem moldar o século XXI. As estruturas gigantescas aqui foram construídas em ritmo acelerado. Grande parte do Parque Industrial de Big Data de Bayin, densamente construído, foi formada em apenas dois anos. Isso demonstra a capacidade de construção rápida da China. Ventos fortes, sol intenso e vastos espaços abertos proporcionam à região acesso a energia verde barata e abundantes recursos de terra. Ulanqab faz parte da visão de Pequim de expandir rapidamente sua infraestrutura de dados. Essa é uma prioridade fundamental para o governo chinês, que vê a IA como um motor de crescimento crucial para sua economia em desaceleração, em meio a uma população em declínio. “A China abriu os braços para a IA”, disse o presidente chinês Xi Jinping em uma conferência global sobre inteligência artificial em Xangai, em julho passado. Ele mencionou iniciativas para integrar a IA em diversas áreas, da saúde aos eletrodomésticos, e elogiou os esforços para integrar a IA na indústria como um dos destaques da modernização da China. Segundo estatísticas oficiais, mais de 700 milhões de pessoas na China utilizam atualmente IA. O plano de integrar a IA na manufatura, na indústria e no cotidiano também exige enorme poder computacional. No mês passado, a China anunciou um plano de US$ 560 bilhões para expandir rapidamente sua infraestrutura de informação nos próximos cinco anos. Empresas privadas de tecnologia também estão aumentando seus investimentos em infraestrutura de IA, embora ainda estejam muito atrás de suas contrapartes do Vale do Silício, nos EUA. Segundo a empresa de pesquisa Rhodium Group, o investimento total de empresas chinesas listadas na bolsa nesse setor dobrará este ano, chegando a aproximadamente US$ 139 bilhões. No entanto, esse valor ainda representa menos de um quinto dos US$ 800 bilhões investidos em data centers de IA por empresas americanas. As empresas chinesas também enfrentam outro desafio sério: o fornecimento limitado de hardware de ponta para equipar data centers. As proibições de exportação dos EUA restringem o acesso aos melhores chips de IA, como alguns modelos da Nvidia e da AMD, enquanto a China também limita as importações de alguns chips de desempenho inferior. Os fabricantes nacionais de chips estão correndo para alcançar a concorrência, mas a tecnologia ainda está atrás da dos EUA, e o fornecimento dos modelos mais avançados continua escasso. "Considerando o custo total de construção de um centro de dados, os chips são o fator mais importante, e a China simplesmente não tem chips suficientes", disse Nick Corvino, pesquisador da Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Você também pode gostar No entanto, o que a China não tem em termos de chips e capital de investimento pode ser compensado por outra vantagem: eletricidade abundante e acessível, grande parte da qual é energia verde. Fontes de energia em excesso Enquanto os centros de dados com alto consumo de energia pressionam a rede elétrica dos EUA, a China adicionou capacidade de geração de energia entre 2022 e 2025 equivalente à capacidade total de todas as fontes de energia industrial dos EUA até o final de 2025. A China também possui mais energia verde do que necessita. O excedente de energia verde que o país desperdiçará nos primeiros seis meses de 2026 é suficiente para abastecer todo o México por um ano. A China quer aproveitar esse excedente de energia para alimentar centros de dados, localizados principalmente em áreas rurais do oeste, onde há muita luz solar, vento e vastas extensões de terra. Essa estratégia também impulsiona o setor de tecnologia verde da China, conhecido como "Dados no Oriente, Computação no Ocidente". De acordo com uma estratégia implementada pela primeira vez em 2022, a China planejou oito centros nacionais de computação, incluindo vários no oeste do país, além de 10 clusters nacionais de data centers. O mais recente plano quinquenal de desenvolvimento econômico do país reforça ainda mais essa orientação para a conectividade, prevendo o desenvolvimento coordenado da infraestrutura de computação com energia limpa. A disponibilidade abundante de energia também pode ajudar a China a compensar as limitações de desempenho de seus chips nacionais. Fabricantes de chips chineses, como a Huawei, estão combinando múltiplos clusters de chips para criar poder computacional equivalente ao de tecnologias mais avançadas. Segundo analistas, essa solução pode ser eficiente para algumas tarefas, mas consome significativamente mais energia. No entanto, especialistas argumentam que, mesmo com energia abundante, a visão de Pequim ainda apresenta limitações. artigo.texto: - The companies are developing the new module because their customers are asking for it - Customers want to embrace more powerful technology for AI workloads with something they’re familiar with - The new modules will increase bandwidth density from 200 Gbps-per-lane to 400 Gbps-per-lane. OCP GLOBAL SUMMIT, SAN JOSE, CALIFORNIA — Cisco and Nvidia this week unveiled plans to develop an ultra-dense small form factor pluggable (USFP) optic module for AI data centers. The USFP is capable of 400 Gbps-per-lane and is expected to deliver 4x the bandwidth density and 1.3x the power efficiency of 200 Gbps-per-lane optics. The companies are developing the USFP because their hyperscaler and neocloud customers are asking for it. The customers want to extend their use of octal small form factor (OSFP) modules but scale from 200 Gbps-per-lane to 400 Gbps-per-lane. With USFP, they can embrace next-generation optical technology for AI workloads without overhauling their data center infrastructure. Fierce asked Will Eatherton, Cisco SVP of Engineering, to break down all this information for us. He said pluggable modules are used in AI data centers to connect servers — which house the GPUs — to the switches. The modules “have the fiber optic pigtail coming out of them, and these plug into both servers as well as into the switches, and then the optic runs between, and that's how you connect up your cluster of hundreds of thousands to millions of GPUs,” he said. The current OSFP technology is topping out, and data centers need an upgrade for the future. In terms of the increase in “lanes,” this refers to the tiny copper pathways that carry electrical signals between the chip and the optical module. Eatherton said others are working on different solutions to increase bandwidth for pluggable optic modules in data centers. For instance, Arista and Broadcom are working on a solution called XPO that involves liquid cooling going to the module. And co-packaged optics (CPO) is another alternative. But Eatherton said Cisco has gotten feedback from its customers that what they really want is something that's like the old thing, but in the next generation. For their USFP, Cisco and Nvidia will work with a variety of vendors. “These modules will have massive engineering,” said Eatherton. “You have an ecosystem. So, what we're announcing is we have simulated and tested and are ready for this module to move into the next stage. And Cisco and Nvidia will champion it.” They will work with connector vendors and then go through a process of forming an open standard. And that’s why they announced the new product at the Open Compute Project (OCP) event, because OCP is all about open technologies that aren't proprietary or locked in. Interestingly, even though Cisco and Nvidia are working together, and Arista and Broadcom are working on the competing standard XPO, Eatherton said that ultimately, everyone will probably support both standards just to cover their bases in terms of providing customers whichever product they want. Although Cisco and Nvidia are not giving specifics about roadmaps or timelines for their USFP, Eatherton said everything is moving so fast it will take a matter of months, not years. Its target market for OSFP are the AI hyperscalers, neoclouds, telcos around the world that are creating sovereign AI clouds, and even high end-enterprises. artigo.texto: SAN ANTONIO – Residents gathered at Northwest Vista College on Tuesday to voice concerns about data center development in San Antonio and discuss what regulations city leaders should consider as they prepare to update the city’s land development rules. The town hall, hosted by District 6 Councilman Ric Galvan, the Greater Edwards Aquifer Alliance and Public Citizen, focused on issues including water use, electricity demand, noise, zoning and the effects of data centers on nearby neighborhoods. The meeting also gave residents an opportunity to learn about the city’s process for updating its Unified Development Code and share feedback on proposed data center regulations. The city’s Development Services Department is drafting regulations for data centers, with City Council expected to vote on the rules in the near future. Randy Sipe said residents need more notice about proposed projects before permits are approved and construction begins. “When you first notice them, it’s too late to do anything because I’ve been to some meetings before and unfortunately the permits are done and over,” Sipe said. “So once they break ground, there is no stopping them.” Luis Leon said he is concerned about how data center development could affect future generations, particularly access to water and electricity costs. “I’m concerned about the future of my descendants,” Leon said. “I want to know that they’re going to be OK, that they’re going to have water and the cost of electricity.” Residents also discussed where data centers should be allowed, how noise should be controlled and what requirements developers should meet. Potential policy changes discussed at the meeting included establishing a clear, updated definition of a data center, revisiting zoning qualifications, strengthening site plan requirements and updating fire and building codes. Galvan said San Antonio has just under 30 data centers within city limits, with 18 or 19 located in District 6. “A little under 30 data centers here in San Antonio city limits, with 18-19 of them here in District 6,” Galvan said. “We’ve seen them grow over time with rapid development over the last 15 years.” Galvan said the city and its residents need to understand how local policies could affect future projects and the communities where they are built. “It’s incumbent on us to make sure we’re understanding what’s going on and how local policies can help impact some of the developments here so our communities aren’t left behind,” he said. Organizers said the town hall was intended to bring more residents, particularly those on the far West Side and in District 6, into discussions about data center development. Annalisa Peace, executive director of the Greater Edwards Aquifer Alliance, said she hopes the city’s development code will be updated to address the growth of large-scale data centers. “We hope that the City will be amending the UDC to accommodate new hyperscale data centers with regulations that best serve the citizens of San Antonio,” Peace said. No official decisions were made at Tuesday’s citizen town hall. The feedback comes as the city works to develop regulations for data centers and prepares for further City Council consideration of updates to the Unified Development Code. Read also:

artigo.texto: The companies will examine the feasibility of running the vessel’s generators as a single, connected power system rather than in isolated groups. Known as closed-bus operations, this approach could reduce the number of engines needed to run at a given time. Combined with energy storage systems, it could help optimize generator use, reduce emissions, and strengthen power-plant resilience during offshore drilling operations. “Offshore drilling units have complex power demands, and the safe integration of energy storage requires a detailed understanding of the vessel, its operating profile and its power system. ABS is proud to support Constellation as it evaluates practical energy storage technologies for its fleet,” said Matt Tremblay, ABS Senior Vice President, Global Markets. Separately at the conference, ABS presented Constellation with an approval in principle (AIP) for its design of a fuel processor for the Laguna Star drillship. The system is designed to emulsify water with fuel inline, ahead of the engine, with the goal of reducing fuel consumption and emissions. “Constellation sees disruptive technologies as a key tool for accelerating the decarbonization of its operations. ABS’s recognition reinforces the technical robustness of these initiatives and their contribution to the commitments established in our ESG 2030 Plan,” said Leonardo Guimarães, Constellation Chief Technology Officer. From electrification to new approaches for fuel and energy efficiency, offshore drilling contractors are looking for practical ways to reduce emissions without compromising uptime. ABS continues to work with offshore energy operators across this range of technologies, supporting projects from early feasibility studies through class approval.
