artigo.texto: Brasil ganha espaço na corrida global por data centers e IA A expansão da inteligência artificial está acelerando investimentos em infraestrutura computacional em diferentes regiões. Na União Europeia, a Comissão lançou em 2026 um programa para criar até sete giga fábricas de IA, apoiado por até € 10 bilhões em recursos públicos e nacionais, com expectativa de mobilizar ao menos € 20 bilhões em capital privado. Nos Estados Unidos, o projeto Stargate avança na expansão da capacidade de data centers para IA. Nesse cenário de disputa global por processamento e energia, o Brasil reúne atributos como matriz elétrica predominantemente renovável, novos incentivos e uma cadeia industrial capaz de participar desse mercado. A corrida global pela inteligência artificial deixou de acontecer apenas no desenvolvimento de modelos e aplicações. À medida que o uso da tecnologia cresce, aumenta também a necessidade de servidores, chips, armazenamento, conectividade e energia para processar grandes volumes de dados. Os data centers, responsáveis por concentrar parte dessa infraestrutura computacional, ganham importância estratégica nesse cenário. Em setembro de 2026, o Fórum Econômico Mundial mostrou a dimensão desse movimento: 97% dos economistas-chefes consultados esperam aumento da adoção de IA nos 12 meses seguintes, enquanto 78% avaliam que os investimentos em data centers contribuirão significativamente para o crescimento econômico global. Esse avanço amplia a disputa entre países capazes de oferecer energia, conectividade e condições para investimentos de longo prazo. O Brasil entra nessa discussão com um diferencial relevante: a composição de sua matriz elétrica. Segundo o Balanço Energético Nacional 2026, da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), 86,8% da oferta interna de eletricidade brasileira em 2025 veio de fontes renováveis. No mesmo ano, as fontes eólica e solar fotovoltaica responderam juntas por 26,4% da geração nacional. O ambiente regulatório também começou a acompanhar essa demanda. Sancionado em setembro de 2026, o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata) prevê incentivos para a instalação, modernização e expansão dessas estruturas, além de estabelecer contrapartidas relacionadas ao uso de energia limpa, à eficiência hídrica, à pesquisa e desenvolvimento e à oferta de capacidade ao mercado interno. O Ministério da Fazenda informa ainda que cerca de 60% dos dados dos brasileiros estão atualmente armazenados fora do país, indicando espaço para ampliar a capacidade nacional de armazenamento e processamento de dados. A oportunidade, porém, não está restrita às empresas que constroem ou operam data centers. Essas instalações dependem de uma cadeia formada por equipamentos elétricos, sistemas de energia, componentes eletrônicos, refrigeração, automação, conectividade e serviços especializados. Estudo da Agência Brasileira de Desenvolvimento Industrial (ABDI) estima em aproximadamente R$ 53,2 milhões o investimento de capital por megawatt instalado em data centers no Brasil e aponta que hardware e software representam quase 62% desse investimento. O país já possui uma base industrial relevante em segmentos relacionados a essa infraestrutura: segundo a Abinee, a indústria eletroeletrônica brasileira faturou cerca de R$ 272 bilhões em 2025, incluindo R$ 52 bilhões em equipamentos industriais, R$ 31,7 bilhões em geração, transmissão, distribuição e armazenamento de energia elétrica, R$ 15,1 bilhões em componentes elétricos e eletrônicos e R$ 15 bilhões em materiais elétricos de instalação. Esses números não representam demanda exclusiva de data centers, mas ajudam a dimensionar a capacidade produtiva existente em setores que podem disputar projetos e fornecimentos à medida que novos investimentos em infraestrutura digital avancem no país. O crescimento dessas oportunidades também aumenta as exigências de gestão para indústrias em expansão. Mais pedidos, fornecedores, materiais, estoques e capacidade produtiva elevam o volume de informações que precisa circular entre diferentes áreas da empresa. O SAP Business One, sistema ERP desenvolvido para empresas em expansão, integra processos de finanças, compras, estoque, vendas, relacionamento com clientes, relatórios e análises em uma mesma estrutura. "A expansão de uma nova cadeia tecnológica pode abrir oportunidades para empresas industriais, mas crescer de forma sustentável exige que a gestão acompanhe esse avanço. Quanto maior a complexidade da operação, maior a necessidade de integrar informações para que produção, estoque, compras e finanças trabalhem a partir da mesma visão do negócio", afirma Marcelo Furtado, Head de Tecnologia da Upper. Com mais de 20 anos de atuação no mercado de tecnologia empresarial, a Upper implementa o SAP Business One e atua em projetos de gestão integrada para empresas em crescimento. Nesse cenário, sistemas ERP podem apoiar a organização dos processos e das informações necessárias para que o aumento de escala não reduza a visibilidade sobre a operação. Para saber mais informações, basta acessar: www.uppertools.com.br.

artigo.texto: The AI Data Center Reckoning: Why Infrastructure Must Earn Its Social License Something fundamental is breaking in the data center world, and it's not just a technical problem. It's becoming a social and political one. October 13, 2026 The AI Data Center Reckoning: Why Infrastructure Must Earn Its Social License Something fundamental is breaking in the data center world, and it's not just a technical problem. It's becoming a social and political one. For decades, data centers operated quietly in the background of modern life. They were infrastructure in the truest sense: essential, reliable, and largely invisible. Communities welcomed them as economic engines that brought jobs and tax revenue without the noise, traffic, or pollution of traditional industry. Then AI arrived and changed everything. AI data centers consume vastly more power, not incrementally more, but orders of magnitude more. They can draw enormous volumes of water for cooling. They require utility infrastructure upgrades that strain local grids. And they're proliferating at a pace that's catching regulators, utilities, and communities off guard. The result is something the industry hasn't faced before: organized resistance. Local and national governments are imposing moratoriums. Utility commissions are questioning grid capacity. Environmental groups are raising alarms about water consumption and carbon emissions. Data centers are losing their social license to operate, and the industry needs solutions that address the root causes, not just the symptoms. Why Social License Demands Converged Architecture The social license crisis stems from a fundamental inefficiency in how data center infrastructure has traditionally been designed. Power, backup systems, and cooling are engineered independently and assembled only during construction. This siloed approach creates cascading inefficiencies that communities can see and feel. Power passes through multiple conversion stages, losing energy as heat at each step. Cooling systems respond slowly to load changes because they lack real-time visibility into compute demand. Energy storage sits idle until a utility outage occurs, providing no benefit during normal operation. The cumulative result is facilities that consume more power, use more water, and place greater strain on local infrastructure than necessary. When a community faces rising electricity rates or water restrictions while a data center down the road operates inefficiently, the backlash is predictable and justified. Incremental improvements won't solve this. The industry needs a fundamental rethinking of infrastructure design, and converged architecture provides a framework for doing exactly that. The Four-in-One Solution Converged architecture integrates power distribution, energy storage, and thermal management as a unified platform from the outset. Midea, working with Clou Electronics, has developed a four-in-one solution that demonstrates how this integration addresses the social license challenge directly. The system combines four critical components into a single coordinated architecture: - Power Supply Integration - Rather than treating power distribution as a separate system, the converged platform minimizes conversion stages, reducing energy loss and waste heat generation from the start. - Active Energy Storage - Instead of backup batteries that sit idle, the system uses energy storage to actively buffer demand spikes in real time. This reduces peak load on the grid, smoothing the facility's impact on local utility infrastructure and making it a better grid citizen. - Magnetic Levitation Cold Source - Traditional chillers rely on mechanical bearings that create friction and consume parasitic energy. Magnetic levitation technology eliminates physical contact in rotating components, using magnetic fields for suspension. This cuts energy consumption in the cooling plant itself while extending equipment life and reducing maintenance requirements. - Liquid-Cooled CDU - The liquid cooling distribution unit (CDU) is designed for higher-temperature operation and near-closed-loop water usage. By integrating with the magnetic levitation cold source and coordinating with real-time compute activity, the system dramatically reduces water consumption compared to conventional evaporative cooling approaches. The key differentiator is integration. These components aren't simply installed in the same facility; they're designed to work together from the ground up. The control systems coordinate across power, storage, and cooling. The thermal interfaces optimize heat transfer. The power buffering responds to actual compute demand, not ambient temperature changes. Magnetic CDU: The Efficiency Foundation As data centers face increasing demands from high-density computing and AI workloads, traditional cooling systems struggle to keep pace. Midea's Magnetic CDU offers a transformative approach to thermal management, combining exceptional energy efficiency with operational simplicity and reduced space requirements. The Magnetic CDU delivers outstanding energy performance that directly impacts operational costs. With a Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.1 or lower, facilities can achieve substantial reductions in electricity consumption compared to conventional cooling systems. The unit's intelligent free cooling capabilities maximize the use of ambient conditions, further reducing energy costs while maintaining optimal operating temperatures for all equipment types. Designed for versatility, the system adapts to diverse cooling requirements with adjustable water temperatures, supporting everything from traditional servers to the latest high-performance computing chips. The unit seamlessly switches between cooling modes in seconds, ensuring stable temperatures even during sudden load changes—critical for preventing equipment stress and maintaining uptime. artigo.texto: More data centers headed to San Antonio. City Council will vote on data center regulations SAN ANTONIO - Tx — The debate over data centers popping up here in San Antonio and all throughout Texas has prompted calls of regulation from city leaders and the community. Tonight District 6 Councilman Ric Galvan hosted a town hall meeting to hear from the community before city council votes on two proposals to regulate data centers. Proposal 1 will automatically permit new data centers as long as they are within certain zoning districts that are at least 500 feet away from residential homes, schools, daycares, assisted living facilities, and hospitals. Proposal 1 would not require a vote from city council; however, Proposal 2 would require a city council vote. Proposal 2 would also give the community an opportunity to make public comments before the data center would be approved. Public commenters at Tuesday’s town hall meeting voiced their concerns. “After hearing what everyone said today it sounds like Proposal 2 needs to be implemented. We have three hospitals in this area. What’s going to happen to the ICU when the electricity goes out, and their generators are not enough?” Councilman Galvan says he is also advocating for data centers to only be allowed to use recycled water. The District 6 Councilman says he supports Proposal 2. “I think primarily what we should be looking towards is that every data center that comes to San Antonio goes before City Council for a full vote.” City Council will vote on the two proposals on Oct. 29.

artigo.texto: Acordo entre YOU.ON Energia e HyperStrong combina tecnologia chinesa com engenharia brasileira e busca espaço nos primeiros leilões de baterias de grande porte do país O Brasil está prestes a abrir uma nova frente no setor elétrico, e uma empresa nacional decidiu se unir a uma gigante chinesa para disputar esse mercado. A YOU.ON Energia e a HyperStrong firmaram um acordo para oferecer sistemas de armazenamento em baterias de grande porte, capazes de guardar eletricidade e fornecê-la à rede quando necessário. A parceria, anunciada em 6 de outubro de 2026, tem como principal objetivo participar das oportunidades comerciais relacionadas aos leilões de armazenamento previstos para dezembro. A iniciativa surge em um momento de expansão da energia solar e eólica, quando o país enfrenta novos desafios para equilibrar geração e consumo de eletricidade. Empresa brasileira aposta em tecnologia chinesa para entrar na disputa por baterias gigantes O acordo foi assinado no final de setembro entre a YOU.ON Energia e a HyperStrong International USA Corp., subsidiária do grupo chinês Beijing HyperStrong Technology. - Engie fecha acordo com indústria brasileira para usar energia de sete usinas solares no RN, com 340,5 MW e redução projetada de R$ 10 milhões por ano na conta de luz - Cemig abre edital de R$ 150 milhões para indústrias, condomínios e prefeituras em Minas Gerais; pela primeira vez, projetos podem incluir baterias para armazenar energia solar - Quatro usinas solares da Rio Alto na Paraíba têm desligamento comercial aprovado pela CCEE por multas não pagas; empresa invoca recuperação extrajudicial, mas pedido é rejeitado - Funai pede suspensão das licenças de duas hidrelétricas em Santa Catarina e abre disputa que envolve 20 usinas nos rios Chapecó e Chapecozinho, com potencial estimado em quase 550 MW Pela estratégia anunciada, a fabricante chinesa fornecerá os sistemas de armazenamento, conhecidos como BESS, enquanto a empresa brasileira ficará responsável pela engenharia, integração dos equipamentos, serviços técnicos e assistência local. Segundo informações divulgadas pela pv magazine Brasil, os equipamentos da HyperStrong deverão chegar ao país já montados e testados pela fabricante. A proposta é combinar a escala industrial chinesa com a experiência brasileira na implantação de sistemas elétricos, reduzindo riscos operacionais e oferecendo soluções competitivas aos investidores. Leilões de dezembro podem abrir caminho para uma nova indústria no Brasil A parceria foi estruturada especialmente para os dois leilões de reserva de capacidade previstos para dezembro de 2026. De acordo com a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (ANEEL), o primeiro certame está programado para 2 de dezembro e será destinado a sistemas que atendam às exigências de fabricação nacional. O segundo, previsto para 4 de dezembro, permitirá a participação de soluções que não cumpram esse requisito específico. Os projetos deverão oferecer potência mínima de 30 megawatts e capacidade de fornecimento durante quatro horas. Os contratos terão duração de 15 anos, com início do atendimento previsto para agosto de 2028. Mais de 6 mil projetos mostram o tamanho da corrida pelo armazenamento Os números divulgados pelo governo ajudam a dimensionar o interesse das empresas nesse mercado. Segundo a Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), foram cadastrados 6.091 projetos de armazenamento, somando 296.807 MW de potência para os leilões de 2026. O volume representa um recorde de cadastramentos para certames do setor elétrico brasileiro e demonstra o interesse dos investidores pelas oportunidades que poderão surgir. Entretanto, os números correspondem a projetos cadastrados, não a empreendimentos aprovados ou contratos garantidos. A capacidade efetivamente contratada dependerá das etapas de habilitação e dos resultados dos leilões. Gigante chinesa afirma ter mais de 400 projetos de baterias espalhados pelo mundo A HyperStrong chega à parceria com uma operação internacional consolidada. Fundada em 2011, a companhia abriu capital na Bolsa de Xangai em janeiro de 2025 e atua no desenvolvimento e na integração de sistemas de armazenamento de energia. Segundo dados apresentados pela própria fabricante, a empresa ultrapassou 400 projetos implementados e 70 gigawatts-hora (GWh) de capacidade acumulada instalada até agosto de 2026. A companhia também informa possuir capacidade anual de produção superior a 70 GWh, apoiada por cinco bases industriais na China. Apesar dessa estrutura, a parceria não inclui, até o momento, anúncio de construção de uma fábrica da HyperStrong no Brasil. Conteúdo nacional será um dos principais desafios da parceria Um dos aspectos mais importantes do acordo envolve as exigências brasileiras de conteúdo local. A YOU.ON já aparece na lista de fornecedores cadastrados pelo Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), na categoria de empresa de engenharia. Contudo, o próprio BNDES esclarece que esse credenciamento inicial representa aproximadamente 15% do percurso necessário para a obtenção do código Finame de um sistema completo. A instituição exige a comprovação de processos produtivos realizados no Brasil, não sendo suficiente importar equipamentos e realizar apenas atividades comerciais. As empresas informaram que a solução conjunta envolverá dois componentes de conteúdo local, mas ainda não divulgaram quais serão esses itens nem o percentual de nacionalização previsto. Empresa brasileira já participou de projeto pioneiro de baterias em São Paulo A YOU.ON possui experiência em armazenamento de grande porte no Brasil. A companhia participou da implantação do sistema de baterias instalado na subestação de Registro, no litoral sul de São Paulo, empreendimento desenvolvido para a ISA Energia Brasil, antiga ISA CTEEP. O projeto possui potência de 30 MW e capacidade de fornecimento de 60 MWh durante duas horas, conforme os dados da transmissora. A instalação ajuda a atender os períodos de maior demanda elétri

artigo.texto: No Chile, a ENGIE inaugurou 160 contêineres de baterias em infraestrutura reservada à expansão térmica. O BESS Lile custou US$ 174 milhões, armazena 802 MWh e pode atender o equivalente a mais de 84 mil casas por até cinco horas. O que estava reservado para ampliar a geração térmica de um complexo industrial no norte do Chile agora abriga uma bateria de escala incomum: 160 contêineres, 40 equipamentos de suporte e capacidade de armazenar 802 MWh de eletricidade. A ENGIE Chile colocou o BESS Lile em operação comercial em Mejillones, na região de Antofagasta, após investir US$ 174 milhões. O empreendimento tem 142 MW de potência e pode devolver eletricidade ao sistema chileno por até cinco horas. Segundo a empresa, isso equivale ao consumo de mais de 84 mil residências durante esse intervalo. A autorização para operar comercialmente foi concedida pelo Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional em 25 de setembro de 2026; a companhia anunciou a conclusão da primeira etapa da reconversão do complexo em 8 de outubro. Um espaço planejado para aumentar a geração térmica recebeu 160 contêineres de baterias O BESS Lile reutiliza a subestação de interconexão, vias internas e áreas de um complexo que havia sido preparado para expansão de geração térmica. São instalações que já tinham acesso ao sistema elétrico, originalmente previstas para uma ampliação da geração a carvão. A antiga estrutura passou a ter outra finalidade sem que todo o complexo térmico fosse convertido de uma só vez. - Pesquisadores da USP usaram simulações de física quântica para investigar 22 espécies químicas e combater falhas em baterias de sódio que prometem formar camada protetora contra dendritos que reduzem a vida útil - Grécia inaugura parque de baterias de € 50 milhões e 200 MWh em Tessalônica, com armazenamento diário equivalente à recarga de 3 mil carros elétricos e reforço à rede elétrica - Peru conecta mais de 136 mil painéis solares no deserto de Nasca e forma complexo de 403,52 MW com dois parques eólicos, unindo sol e vento na mesma região de Ica - Estudo com 88 mil unidades consumidoras de energia solar por assinatura registrou inadimplência média de 17% e alerta para riscos da abertura do mercado livre no Brasil As baterias ficam distribuídas em 160 contêineres, acompanhados por 40 conjuntos elétricos de apoio. O parque funciona como sistema independente de armazenamento, conhecido como stand-alone: recebe eletricidade da rede e pode reinjetá-la quando o operador necessita. Ao contrário de uma usina, o equipamento não gera eletricidade: guarda a energia recebida e a devolve em horários determinados pela operação da rede. São 142 MW de potência, 802 MWh guardados e autonomia de até cinco horas A capacidade final divulgada em 2026 superou a previsão de 140 MW apresentada pela empresa um ano antes. Os 142 MW indicam a potência que o parque pode entregar ou receber. Os 802 MWh representam a quantidade de energia que seus módulos podem guardar. A relação entre potência e capacidade define por quanto tempo as baterias podem fornecer eletricidade. A empresa usa uma referência residencial para traduzir essa capacidade: eletricidade equivalente ao consumo de mais de 84 mil casas durante até cinco horas de fornecimento. Quando há muita produção solar durante o dia, baterias conectadas à rede podem absorver parte dessa energia e devolvê-la após o pôr do sol, quando a geração fotovoltaica diminui. Como o BESS Lile está conectado diretamente à rede, sua carga e descarga dependem da operação do sistema, e não de um parque solar exclusivo no local. O carvão começou a sair de Mejillones no fim de 2025, mas a transformação continua A mudança não começou com os contêineres. Depois de quase três décadas de operação, a ENGIE desligou em 31 de dezembro de 2025 as unidades a carvão CTM1 e CTM2, que tinham juntas 334 MW de capacidade instalada, segundo o relatório anual da companhia. O plano de descarbonização ainda prevê outros equipamentos e retiradas de unidades no mesmo conjunto industrial. Outra unidade da região, a Infraestrutura Energética Mejillones (IEM), está em processo de adaptação para funcionar com gás natural. Em outubro de 2026, a empresa dizia que essa instalação ainda aguardava a entrada em operação comercial após a conversão. A empresa mantém no plano de transformação o futuro encerramento de operações a carvão nas unidades Central Termoeléctrica Andina (CTA) e Central Termoeléctrica Hornitos (CTH). Potência de baterias no Chile saiu de 1,2 GW para 3,2 GW ao longo de 2025 O novo parque entra em uma rede que está mudando rapidamente. Um levantamento do Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional, divulgado em abril, mostrou que a potência de armazenamento em baterias no Chile passou de aproximadamente 1,2 GW para 3,2 GW ao longo de 2025. O mesmo relatório apontou participação conjunta recorde de 46,2% da geração solar e eólica em dezembro de 2025. O órgão também identificou gargalos e atrasos na infraestrutura de transmissão e apontou a necessidade de atualizar regras de operação e remuneração diante do crescimento das baterias. Antes de Lile, a ENGIE colocou mais 251 MW de baterias em operação em agosto Em 28 de agosto de 2026, a companhia informou a entrada em operação comercial de outros dois projetos: BESS Libélula, na região de Santiago, e BESS Los Loros, em Atacama. Juntos, eles adicionaram 251 MW de potência de armazenamento ao sistema chileno, com US$ 283 milhões investidos nessa parte dos empreendimentos. O BESS Libélula dispõe de 203 MW e 1.034 MWh, com 208 contêineres, e integra um projeto que também inclui geração solar. O Los Loros reúne 48 MW e 275,23 MWh junto a uma usina fotovoltaica existente. Lile é diferente: opera como armazenamento independente, dentro de um complexo de origem térmica. Com o início das operações em Mejillones, a ENGIE contabiliza cinco sistemas de baterias que começaram a operar comercialmente em 2026 e informa ter alcançado 803 MW de capacidade instalada nessa tecnologia no Chile. artigo.texto: About one-fifth of the 101 towns and villages in the Adirondack Park have passed moratoriums this year on building battery energy storage systems, and now bans are coming, according to local laws filed with the New York Department of State. The towns of Fort Ann, Gloversville and Forestport, which are all partially within the Adirondack Park, have banned battery systems. The town of St. Armand’s board had passed a ban this summer, but failed to evaluate the local law through the State Environmental Quality Review Act. Supervisor Davina Thurston said the town board is going through that process now and plans to pass the ban again. Twenty-one municipalities in the park have filed local laws since Jan. 1 delaying battery storage builds. The moratoriums range from six months to a year. Several are set to expire if they are not renewed. The state’s quest for more storage Battery energy storage systems are a way for the electric grid to store power for later use. Generally made up of lithium-ion batteries, the systems are intended to help the grid rely less on fossil fuel-using peaker plants, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions. They may also increase the grid’s reliability and reduce the need for infrastructure upgrades. Large battery system fires in New York have spooked municipalities, even with the state’s updated fire code. The new fire code requires developers to fund a peer review of their projects, including inspections with the local permitting authority, to train local fire departments and to provide a battery fire expert on site within four hours of any fire. New York’s goal is to have 6 gigawatts of energy storage online by 2030, but the reality of that is looking grim. As of Aug. 31, the state’s total storage capacity was about 576 megawatts. New York has led a national, developer-tracked survey of moratoriums. The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority has been sending representatives to Adirondack Park Agency and municipal meetings to help alleviate fire fears and answer questions. St. Armand’s ban Energy developer Carson Power had an initial proposal to install a 20-megawatt facility near the Mount Pisgah Ski Area in the town of St. Armand. In March, the town passed a one-year moratorium on battery storage builds. In June, the board decided to pass a ban without going through the State Environmental Quality Review Act. Thurston said the town’s attorney is assisting in getting the law reviewed under the act and is moving forward with an official ban. Jennifer Manierre, the director of clean energy and siting at NYSERDA, visited the town on Sept. 1 and spoke about batteries’ benefits and the safeguards the state now has in place to protect public health and the environment, meeting minutes show. Residents were still concerned about a potential battery fire, especially in the area of the proposed project. Thurston said she felt “the appropriate action is to move forward with a town-wide ban on battery energy storage systems,” according to meeting minutes. In an interview on Thursday, Thurston said the ban would prevent the Carson Power project from being built. She had invited Carson Power to the Sept. 1 meeting, but they declined, she added. Carson Power did not respond to Adirondack Explorer’s request for comment. Dannemora update In Dannemora, Supervisor Joey Varin remains openminded to battery energy storage. He’s attended classes and seminars related to the storage systems and fires. Varin has the beginnings of a proposal to put a battery energy storage system on the tailings pile of the former mining operation at Lyon Mountain. The developer examining the site is Brookfield Renewable Partners. The business is currently in talks with the utility company, New York State Electric and Gas, about potentially upgrading a nearby substation, Varin said. He is planning to host a public meeting about it around the beginning of next year once Brookfield has more information. He thinks the project is at an ideal site, outside of the hamlet in an old sand pit. “I’ve been asked by a number of people outside of our area to put a moratorium on,” Varin said. “I said no. … We’re just gathering more and more knowledge, educating ourselves the best way we can of understanding all we can about it. When the time comes, we’ll make sure our residents are totally educated on the process and start those general information sessions with our residents.” Moratorium progress and renewals In the town of Northampton, the Adirondack Park Agency (APA) permitted the first large-scale battery energy storage system in the park. It was a 10-megawatt, four-hour system, also proposed by Carson Power. In March, however, the town passed a one-year moratorium on battery system builds. The moratorium was on new projects. The Carson Power project did not appear to be covered. Concerned about battery storage facilities, Northampton resident Sara Will-White sued the town, the APA, Carson Power and the project site’s landowner. A Fulton County state supreme court justice issued a temporary restraining order, delaying the project, but has not yet issued a decision on the lawsuit. In Ticonderoga, a six-month moratorium passed in March is soon ending. Meeting minutes show the town is considering passing an additional six-month moratorium. The town of Indian Lake is in a similar position. It’s unclear from meeting minutes if the town is considering a renewal of its moratorium. Town Supervisor Brian Wells did not return Adirondack Explorer’s inquiry. The town of Hadley’s moratorium is on the cusp of ending, but meeting minutes show the board is working on a renewal.

artigo.texto: CATL expands Seres battery capacity: what it means for Contemporary Amperex Technology stock Published on 10/13/2026 at 09:01 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS - CATL agreed with Seres on October 11, 2026, to expand dedicated battery capacity to more than 20 GWh annually. - The October 11 agreement adds 10 to 12 GWh of annual pack capacity at Seres' Chongqing plant. - Second-quarter 2026 revenue reached CNY 147.8 billion, while net income was CNY 22.5 billion. - The Shenzhen quote was CNY 288.71 on October 13, 2026, 1.24 percent above the 52-week low. Contemporary Amperex Technology stock was quoted at CNY 288.71 on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on October 13, 2026 at 2:45 p.m. CST, as CATL expanded its battery partnership with Seres. The October 11 agreement adds 10 to 12 gigawatt-hours of annual pack capacity and takes dedicated capacity at Seres' Chongqing plant above 20 gigawatt-hours, according to East Asia Brief on October 11, 2026. What 20 GWh means for CATL The Seres project places CATL battery assembly directly inside the vehicle plant. The expansion adds 10 to 12 GWh of annual pack capacity, while the agreement gives CATL a five-year supply framework running through August 2027, East Asia Brief reported. The operating model also locks CATL into Seres' Aito vehicle range, whose cumulative deliveries equipped with CATL batteries have exceeded 1.2 million units, according to the same October 11 report. For CATL, the value is production visibility rather than a disclosed order amount because the companies did not publish construction costs or a commissioning date. Recent results show scale CATL reported CNY 147.8 billion of revenue and CNY 22.5 billion of net income for the second quarter of 2026. Revenue rose 57 percent from CNY 94.2 billion in the second quarter of 2025, while net income increased 37 percent from CNY 16.5 billion, according to Simply Wall St. The comparison also shows the pressure behind the capacity push: second-quarter profit growth trailed revenue growth by 20 percentage points. Simply Wall St reported that the second-quarter profit margin was 15 percent, down from 18 percent a year earlier, while earnings per share exceeded analyst expectations by 2.1 percent. Three dated operating milestones On July 25, 2026, CATL reported second-quarter revenue of CNY 147.8 billion and net income of CNY 22.5 billion. On September 22, 2026, its Debrecen factory began trial production after the company had produced 537,000 battery modules at the site. On October 11, 2026, the Seres agreement lifted the Chongqing plant's planned dedicated capacity above 20 GWh, with each event covered by Simply Wall St and East Asia Brief. Next results come into view CATL's board is scheduled to meet on October 20, 2026, to consider third-quarter results for the nine months ended September 30, according to Futubull. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on October 21, 2026, according to Simply Wall St. Stock stays near its yearly low The Shenzhen quote of CNY 288.71 on October 13, 2026 stood 1.24 percent above the 52-week low of CNY 285.17 and 38.33 percent below the 52-week high of CNY 468.75. CATL's market capitalization was CNY 1.3 trillion on that date, giving the Seres expansion a market setting defined by scale and a wide distance from the yearly high. The continuously updated company information is available through the Market report Shanghai Composite. artigo.texto: Análise: Mercado de carbono expõe desafio brasileiro Enquanto a Europa amplia gradualmente a cobrança sobre emissões de produtos importados, o Brasil ainda define as regras de seu mercado regulado de carbono Exportar aço e alumínio para a União Europeia exigirá cada vez mais atenção às emissões de gases de efeito estufa geradas durante a fabricação desses produtos. Isso porque os europeus começaram a aplicar um mecanismo que atribui um custo à poluição associada às importações. Enquanto essa cobrança será ampliada gradualmente, o Brasil ainda regulamenta seu próprio mercado de carbono, criado por lei em 2024. A diferença entre os dois sistemas poderá se tornar especialmente importante em 2030, quando as regras europeias ficarão mais rigorosas. O CBAM (Mecanismo de Ajuste de Carbono na Fronteira) entrou em sua fase definitiva em janeiro de 2026. Pelo sistema, importadores europeus de produtos como aço e alumínio deverão adquirir certificados que representam as emissões de gases de efeito estufa associadas à fabricação dessas mercadorias. Cada certificado corresponde a uma tonelada de dióxido de carbono equivalente (CO₂e). Embora não seja formalmente um imposto de importação, o CBAM estabelece uma cobrança sobre as emissões de gases de efeito estufa associadas à fabricação de determinados produtos vendidos à União Europeia. O pagamento será feito pelos importadores europeus, que comprarão das autoridades do bloco certificados cujo preço acompanha o mercado regulado de carbono europeu: € 82,32 por tonelada no terceiro trimestre de 2026. Não se trata de créditos do mercado voluntário. As compras começarão em fevereiro de 2027, referentes às importações realizadas em 2026. A cobrança sobre as importações aumentará gradualmente porque a União Europeia está reduzindo as permissões gratuitas de emissão de carbono concedidas às suas próprias indústrias. Essas permissões permitem que as empresas emitam determinada quantidade de gases de efeito estufa sem precisar comprar autorizações no mercado regulado. Em 2029, as indústrias europeias dos setores cobertos pelo CBAM ainda receberão gratuitamente 77,5% das permissões calculadas segundo os critérios do bloco, percentual que cairá para 51,5% em 2030. Isso significa que a redução do benefício, de 22,5% em 2029, chegará a 48,5% no ano seguinte. Essa mesma redução será considerada no cálculo da cobrança sobre os produtos importados, para que fabricantes europeus e estrangeiros estejam sujeitos a condições equivalentes de precificação do carbono. Isso não significa que o importador pagará sobre 48,5% das emissões de cada produto: o desconto é calculado sobre parâmetros de referência europeus, e não sobre as emissões reais. Quanto mais o produto emitir acima desses parâmetros, maior será a cobrança. O artigo 9º do CBAM permite reduzir a cobrança europeia quando o importador comprova que já houve pagamento pelas emissões de carbono no país onde a mercadoria foi produzida. No Brasil, porém, a Lei nº 15.042/2024 estabelece que, no primeiro ciclo do SBCE (Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões), as empresas receberão gratuitamente cotas que autorizam a emissão de determinadas quantidades de gases de efeito estufa. Cada cota corresponde ao direito de emitir uma tonelada de dióxido de carbono equivalente (CO₂e). Como essas autorizações serão inicialmente distribuídas sem cobrança, seu recebimento não representa um pagamento que possa ser descontado da obrigação europeia. Há uma consequência adicional. O artigo 11 da lei brasileira vincula o início da distribuição onerosa às fases de implementação do SBCE. A cobrança pelas cotas deverá ocorrer após o primeiro ciclo de alocação gratuita, na etapa de implementação plena. Assim, mesmo que o mercado comece a operar por volta de 2030, a possibilidade de reconhecer pagamentos brasileiros no CBAM não surgirá automaticamente. O SBCE ainda está em fase de regulamentação. Pela lei, empresas de setores abrangidos pelo sistema que emitam mais de 10 mil toneladas anuais de dióxido de carbono equivalente (CO₂e) deverão informar suas emissões ao governo. Acima de 25 mil toneladas, terão também de comprovar que possuem cotas ou certificados reconhecidos pelo mercado regulado em quantidade suficiente para cobrir suas emissões. Essa obrigação, entretanto, ainda não está em vigor. Consulta pública aberta pelo Ministério da Fazenda em julho propôs iniciar gradualmente o monitoramento das emissões em 2027, sem exigir, nessa etapa, a compra de cotas. A agenda inicial da Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono previa para junho a definição dos setores econômicos sujeitos à regulamentação e a criação da CAREG (Câmara de Assuntos Regulatórios). Esse órgão deverá reunir representantes das atividades reguladas para discutir as regras de funcionamento do mercado, incluindo a distribuição das cotas de emissão. Segundo a ata da reunião do comitê consultivo de 30 de junho, sua constituição ocorrerá somente depois da definição dos setores abrangidos. Isso significa que a demora na conclusão dessa primeira etapa também pode comprometer a formação da Câmara e o avanço das normas seguintes. O governo anunciou a intenção de concluir a regulamentação até dezembro de 2026, mas ainda precisa esclarecer a situação dessas entregas. A prioridade é definir os setores, constituir a CAREG e divulgar um calendário consistente para o primeiro Plano Nacional de Alocação. Também é necessário explicar como as cotas gratuitas serão substituídas gradualmente por mecanismos de precificação efetiva. A indústria precisa conhecer essa trajetória antes de comprometer recursos em instalações e tecnologias que permanecerão em operação muito além de 2030.

artigo.texto: SINEXCEL Completes Power Conversion System Shipment for 100 MW/400 MWh Chile Battery Storage Project SINEXCEL has completed the shipment of all power conversion systems for a 100 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage project in Chile, according to a company press release. The Shenzhen-listed firm said the delivery covers the full order of StellaON 1250K units for RelyEZ Energy Storage Technology Co., Ltd. The project is a four-hour system located in the Atacama region. It is designed to charge when demand is lower and discharge during peak periods, a pattern intended to support grid flexibility and project returns. Delivery Timing and Project Execution SINEXCEL stated that it completed the full power conversion system order on schedule. The company said this helps RelyEZ Energy protect the timetable for transport, installation, commissioning, and grid connection. According to the release, large-scale overseas projects depend on production, inspection, and shipment schedules staying closely aligned with on-site construction. Coordinated delivery is described as reducing uncertainty and helping local teams plan subsequent stages, since delays in a single batch can narrow the construction window for a project of this scale. Equipment Specifications for Atacama Conditions The StellaON 1250K power conversion system is built for environments that can include high temperatures, dust, and sand. SINEXCEL reported a maximum efficiency of 99% and a rated-power efficiency of 98.5% for the unit. The system supports operation from minus 40 degrees Celsius to 60 degrees Celsius, maintains full power output at 55 degrees Celsius, and carries an IP65 protection rating. The company said maintaining rated output in high temperatures can reduce power derating and the need for additional capacity, while higher conversion efficiency limits energy losses across repeated charge-discharge cycles. Service Network and Company Scale Following shipment, the Chilean project moves into on-site installation and commissioning. SINEXCEL said it has a dedicated after-sales team in Latin America and seven service centres across the Americas. Technical requests can receive a response within 30 minutes, backed by round-the-clock support and a seven-day spare-parts guarantee. SINEXCEL reported that it has deployed more than 17 GW of energy storage capacity across over 5,000 projects and works with more than 600 partners in more than 60 countries and regions. The company said it will continue to expand its local operations across Latin America and provide customers with support throughout the project lifecycle. Founded in 2007, SINEXCEL describes itself as a pioneer in energy storage, electric vehicle charging, and power quality solutions. Its disclosed deployments include 17 GW of installed storage, 200,000 electric vehicle DC chargers, and nearly 20 million amperes of active harmonic filters. - 1. artigo.texto: MESA — Dozens of Valley residents shared concerns about data centers with Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes at a town hall in Mesa on Wednesday night. Mayes has called for a temporary moratorium on new data center approvals. “This really has to be dealt with at the statewide level, and that's why I have called for a moratorium for now, so that we can get our hands around the situation,” she told reporters after the town hall. Several speakers spoke out against a data center under construction in Ahwatukee. Menlo Digital is building a 1 million-square-foot hyperscale campus with an onsite power substation with 257 megawatts of power. “This is a very serious health concern for us,” said Kathy Monk, who lives a half mile away from the construction site. She said her family doctor told her people that close to the completed data center will face cardiac and pulmonary issues. “Do you know what he told me?” she told Mayes. “He said, ‘You need to move. You need to move.’ My doctor said that.” Do you have a concern in your community or a news tip? We want to hear from you! Connect with us: share@abc15.com Monk also said the high-pitch frequency emitted from the data center complex could harm people with hearing aids and pacemakers. “It’s toxic,” she said. Other data center opponents said such heavy industrial facilities shouldn’t be allowed in commercial areas located so close to residential areas. “We have talked to the city – our city councilman, the mayor – and it was really depressing, the answers that we got,” another opponent to the Ahwatukee data center said. The city of Phoenix updated its zoning ordinances in 2025 to address data centers, but the Menlo Digital project was approved in 2024, when the data centers were considered similar to an office use, the city told ABC15 in August. Mayes, whose office is investigating the project, said she is considering filing a nuisance lawsuit. She told reporters after the forum that she was concerned about hyperscaled AI data centers like the Menlo Digital campus being built in areas designed for lower-level commercial operations. “And then they are somehow flipping that into this gigantic industrial facility that can give off constant noise ... and possibly constant air pollution, if they're using diesel generators to power them at any time,” Mayes said. “And so there's a lot to be investigated here, I think, with regard to these data centers.” One person, Lisa Everett, spoke in favor of data centers, pointing to the tax dollars paid by the facilities and the number of construction jobs the projects would create. She said she was also concerned about misinformation on data centers. “I understand the frustration. I understand it’s new,” she said. “But I’m asking you, is this just a fashionable thing, to be against data centers? Are we really going to have honest conversations?” Gov. Katie Hobbs, a Democrat like Mayes, has said the state should develop standards for data centers but does not support a moratorium. Mayes told ABC15 she will be talking with the governor about her proposal. “I'm going to lobby her. I'm going to advocate for my position,” she said. “I'm going to be working with legislators.” Hobbs said she hopes the Legislature will pass legislation addressing data centers next year. “And I think it'll be a bipartisan bill,” she said. “I think you're going to see Republicans and Democrats come together on this issue.” “If you like your tech and your phone and your computer and the stuff you can use that for, you probably think data centers are important,” he said during his debate with Mayes last month. Mayes said she plans to hold more town halls on data centers, including in Ahwatukee.

artigo.texto: Enlight Renewable Energy (TASE: ENLT; NASDAQ: ENLT) and ENERTRAG SE announced yesterday the official start of construction work on the Bertikow battery storage project in Brandenburg, following the ground-breaking ceremony held on 13 October at the project site. The ceremony was attended by representatives from Enlight, ENERTRAG and 50Hertz, as well as politicians, partners and local residents. Bertikow is a large-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) with a capacity of 200 MW and an energy storage capacity of around 840 MWh. It is a joint project between Enlight and ENERTRAG. The project is situated directly next to the Bertikow substation in the municipality of Uckerfelde; the land rights and grid connection have been secured. The transition from the development phase to the construction phase has been completed, and construction work is already underway. Commissioning is currently scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2027, with commercial operation due to commence in the first half of 2028. Once it becomes operational, Bertikow is expected to participate in the German day-ahead and intraday energy markets, as well as in the balancing energy markets, and to help balance electricity supply and demand by providing flexibility. A seven-year off-take agreement has been signed with EDF Trading for part of the storage capacity. The agreement marks Enlight’s first BESS off-take transaction in Europe and signals the company’s entry into the German battery storage market. The facility is being optimised by Entrix. Osborne Clarke acted as legal advisers to Enlight and ENERTRAG in connection with the acquisition. Comments from the companies Marko Liposcak, Managing Director of Enlight Europe: “As renewable energy continues to expand across Europe, large-scale energy storage systems are becoming increasingly important for the flexibility and reliability of electricity grids. Bertikow is a prime example of how such projects can help meet these changing requirements, whilst further strengthening Enlight’s presence in the European energy storage market. Together with ENERTRAG, we are delighted to mark the start of construction and to take another important step towards the commissioning of this project.” Dr Gunar Hering, CEO of ENERTRAG: “Bertikow is proof that the energy transition works in practice. We store surplus electricity from renewable energy sources and feed it into the grid precisely when it is most urgently needed: in this way, we provide reliable green electricity round the clock and keep the value added within the region.” Stefan Schlüter, Head of the DACH Region at EDF Trading: “The expansion of battery storage across Europe is driving demand for increasingly sophisticated commercial solutions. This agreement combines revenue security with commercial flexibility and demonstrates how innovative procurement structures can support the roll-out of large-scale storage facilities. We look forward to working with Enlight, ENERTRAG and Entrix on the Bertikow project.” Constantin Nicklas, Chief Revenue Officer at Entrix: “There need not be a conflict of objectives between bankability and earnings potential. Together with ENERTRAG, Enlight and EDF Trading, we have created a structure that maximises the returns from Bertikow without compromising our partners’ risk profile or financing requirements.”

artigo.texto: Recently, the "Hydrogen Wind Series portable hydrogen power generation equipment" independently developed by Guangdong Huachen Hydrogen Energy Co., Ltd. is about to be officially released. As the first product in this series, the world's first 200W portable hydrogen power generation equipmentwas officially released at the "Five New" power equipment technology exhibition and new-type power system equipment upgrade technology conference during the 28th China (Shenzhen) International Hi-Tech Fair. Innovative hybrid energy architecture addresses mobile energy storage endurance pain points In scenarios such as emergency rescue, power repair, communication support, field operations, and outdoor mobile power consumption, energy supply is often constrained by multiple factors including fixed power grid coverage, equipment endurance, refueling efficiency, and transportation conditions. Especially in long-duration continuous operation environments, traditional mobile energy storage equipment mainly relies on increasing battery capacity to improve endurance, but the resulting increases in weight, volume, and charging time can also affect equipment mobility and usage efficiency. To address these needs, the Hydrogen Wind Series portable hydrogen power generation equipment is designed around the concept of "continuous power generation," using coordinated operation of multiple energy systems to build a mobile energy solution suitable for off-grid scenarios. The product adopts ahybrid energy architecture in which aluminum-based energy storage materials, hydrogen fuel cells, and lithium batteries work in coordination. Among them, aluminum-based energy storage materials handle energy storage functions, hydrogen fuel cells are responsible for energy conversion, and lithium batteries respond to equipment start-stop, instantaneous loads, and power fluctuations, achieving coordinated operation across energy storage, power generation conversion, and stable output. At the same time, the product adopts a modular refueling approach, enabling rapid refueling by replacing aluminum-based energy storage materials, and can flexibly configure energy reserves according to different mission durations and actual load requirements, enhancing continuous power generation capability while maintaining equipment portability. First 200W product released, covering diverse civilian and professional scenarios As the first product in the Hydrogen Wind Series, the world's first 200W portable hydrogen power generation equipment is primarily aimed at mobile application scenarios with high requirements for equipment portability, continuous power supply capability, and refueling flexibility. In the civilian sector, the product can serve outdoor travel, mobile office work, drone power supply, and other needs; in professional application fields, it can be further extended to emergency support, power and communication operations, and field operations, providing new power generation solutions for mobile electricity use in different environments. Starting with the 200W product, Guangdong Huachen Hydrogen Energy will continue to improve the Hydrogen Wind Series product lineup around different power levels and application needs, gradually forming a portable hydrogen power generation equipment portfolio covering multiple types of scenarios. Engineering validation continues to advance, safety assurance system refined Moving from laboratory technology to end-use products, engineering validation is a critical step in promoting product application. Currently, Hydrogen Wind Series products have undergone testing and validation around application scenarios such as emergency rescue, power repair, communication support, and field operations, with continuous optimization of system stability, safety, and environmental adaptability in complex environments. In terms of safety assurance, the product is equipped with an intelligent monitoring system that provides real-time monitoring of key parameters such as system operating status, temperature, and pressure, and enhances system operational reliability through multiple safety protection mechanisms. At the same time, to meet the demands of outdoor and complex environment applications, the product features targeted designs for wide-temperature-range operation, wind and sand resistance, and dust protection. Guangdong Huachen Hydrogen Energy Co., Ltd. is a hydrogen energy end-user industrialisation platform wholly established by Zhongyun Intelligent Technology (Guangzhou) Co., Ltd., primarily focused on high-end hydrogen energy end-use equipment R&D, scenario-based solutions, and industrialisation applications. The launch of the "Hydrogen Wind Series" portable hydrogen power generation equipment represents an important step for the company in advancing scenario-based, productised, and industrialised applications of hydrogen energy technology.

artigo.texto: CHARLOTTE, N.C., Oct. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Magnera today announced it has entered into a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Army Research Laboratory to evaluate and advance next-generation battery separator technologies, supporting evolving energy requirements across defense, critical infrastructure, and commercial applications. The collaboration will leverage Magnera's OmniSep™ platform, an advanced separator technology engineered to enhance battery performance, safety, and reliability in demanding operating environments. Designed with high ionic conductivity, superior electrolyte wettability, and enhanced thermal stability1, OmniSep™ supports the power, efficiency, and safety requirements of next-generation battery systems. The initiative aligns with the Department of War's growing emphasis on resilient energy, electrification, and assured power for distributed and contested operations. As the military deploys increasingly power-intensive capabilities, including autonomous systems, ISR platforms, electronic warfare, counter-UAS technologies, resilient communications, and directed energy systems, the need for safe, high-performance energy storage continues to grow. Advances in separator technology could help extend operational endurance, enhance system performance, improve safety, and reduce logistical burdens across a broad range of current and future defense applications. "Energy resilience and advanced battery technologies will play an increasingly important role in national security, infrastructure modernization, and the future of mobility," said Curt Begle, Chief Executive Officer of Magnera. "This collaboration is an investment in technologies that can enable the next generation of energy storage solutions. By combining the Army Research Laboratory's research capabilities with Magnera's advanced materials expertise, we have the opportunity to accelerate innovations with potential impact across defense, critical infrastructure, and commercial markets." Designed and manufactured in the United States, OmniSep™ reflects Magnera's commitment to strengthening the nation's advanced manufacturing and materials ecosystem. Leveraging domestic production capabilities and U.S.-sourced raw materials, the platform supports secure, resilient supply chains for mission-critical energy storage technologies while reinforcing American industrial competitiveness. 1 Based on internal testing About Magnera Magnera Corporation (NYSE: MAGN) serves 1,000+ customers worldwide, offering a wide range of material solutions, including components for absorbent hygiene products, protective apparel, wipes, specialty building and construction products, and products serving the food and beverage industry. Leading in iron electrolyte technology According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Flow Battery Stacks market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global flow battery stacks market is entering a decisive growth phase as long-duration energy storage (LDES) shifts from pilot deployments to mainstream grid infrastructure. Flow battery stacks, the modular electrochemical cores of redox flow battery systems, enable independent scaling of power and energy, long cycle life, and inherent safety, making them uniquely suited for storage durations exceeding four hours. Demand is being pulled forward by utility-scale renewable integration, commercial and industrial resilience requirements, and the electrification of remote operations. Vanadium redox flow stacks remain the commercial anchor, while zinc-bromine, iron-chromium, organic, and hybrid chemistries advance toward broader adoption. This report analyzes market size, segmentation, supply chain dynamics, and competitive positioning, providing a data-driven outlook through 2035. It examines how cost reduction, manufacturing scale-up, and policy support for LDES will shape the trajectory of stack demand across five major regions and five end-use sectors. The baseline scenario for the flow battery stacks market through 2035 assumes continued policy support for long-duration energy storage, steady cost declines in stack manufacturing, and accelerating renewable capacity additions. Under this scenario, the market expands at a compound annual growth rate of 18.5% from 2026 to 2035, with the market index rising to 545 by 2035 from a 2025 base of 100. Growth is front-loaded in Asia-Pacific, where utility-scale tenders and manufacturing capacity are concentrated, followed by North America and Europe as grid resilience and decarbonization mandates tighten. Vanadium redox stacks retain the largest share, but zinc-bromine and organic flow chemistries gain ground in cost-sensitive and behind-the-meter applications. Supply chain maturity, membrane and electrode cost reduction, and standardization of stack interfaces are critical enablers. Risks include vanadium price volatility, slower-than-expected policy implementation, and competition from lithium-ion in shorter-duration segments. Overall, the baseline outlook points to a market transitioning from niche to mainstream, with stack manufacturers scaling production and forming strategic partnerships with system integrators and utilities. Utility-scale energy storage is the dominant end-use for flow battery stacks, driven by the need to store excess renewable generation for dispatch during peak demand or low-generation periods. The shift toward longer-duration storage, typically 8 to 24 hours, favors flow battery stacks over lithium-ion due to their scalable energy capacity and low degradation. As utilities gain operational experience, standardizing stack specifications will further reduce costs and drive adoption. Major trends: Procurement of 8+ hour storage systems in renewable-heavy grids, Integration of flow batteries in capacity markets and ancillary services, Growing preference for non-lithium technologies for fire safety and longevity, and Development of large-scale vanadium and zinc-bromine projects. Representative participants: Sumitomo Electric Industries, Rongke Power, VRB Energy, Invinity Energy Systems, and Stryten Energy. In this segment, stacks are integrated into systems that provide 4 to 12 hours of backup, often in combination with solar PV. Demand is particularly strong in regions with unstable grids or high demand charges. Through 2035, adoption will be supported by declining stack costs, financing models such as energy-as-a-service, and corporate sustainability targets. Key indicators include commercial construction activity, power outage frequency, and the spread of time-of-use tariffs. Flow battery stacks offer advantages in safety and cycle life, though competition from lithium-ion remains intense for shorter durations. Current trend: Steady growth as businesses prioritize resilience and energy cost management. Major trends: Rising adoption of behind-the-meter storage for demand charge reduction, Corporate decarbonization commitments driving clean backup power, Modular stack designs enabling scalable C&I installations, and Financing innovations lowering upfront cost barriers. artigo.texto: Nightpeak Energy's Bocanova 2 Battery Storage Project Reaches Financial Close and Commercial Operation Nightpeak Energy reported on October 13, 2026, that its Bocanova 2 battery storage facility in Southeast Texas, sized at 150 MW with a two-hour duration, has achieved both financial close and commercial operation. The company stated the project went into commercial service on September 17, lifting the Bocanova site's total capacity to 300 MW and contributing added flexibility to the ERCOT grid amid surging electricity demand from data centers and other large loads. Located in Brazoria County near the Houston metropolitan area, Bocanova 2 represents the second phase of Nightpeak's battery storage buildout there. Bocanova 1, the initial 150 MW phase, entered commercial operation in August 2025. Tesla's Megapack 2 XL battery storage systems equip the project. It runs under a long-term offtake agreement with an investment-grade counterparty, with financing arranged via a tax equity bridge loan and a construction-to-term loan from MUFG Bank, while U.S. Bank supplied traditional tax equity. Paris Hays, Co-founder and CEO/CDO of Nightpeak Energy, noted that large loads are connecting to the grid at a speed and magnitude that is reshaping how the power sector anticipates new demand. Hays remarked that Texas leads this growth, and addressing it will demand substantial new infrastructure along with resources capable of responding swiftly as conditions shift. Hays further stated that with 300 MW now active at Bocanova, the company is deploying that flexibility in one of the nation's most dynamic power markets, and thanked the City of Alvin, Brazoria County, and the local community for their backing. Founded in 2022, Nightpeak has built and purchased a portfolio exceeding 1 GW of operating and de-risked capacity across gas-fired generation, battery storage, and powered land development, while continuing to push forward an additional pipeline of flexible generation and large-load projects to serve rising U.S. demand. Nightpeak Energy develops, owns, and operates flexible power generation and large-load enablement assets aimed at meeting growing electricity and AI demand while fostering a reliable, lower-carbon electric grid. Using a technology-agnostic strategy spanning gas-fired generation, energy storage, renewables, and large-load project types, the company merges generation and load into integrated solutions for its customers. Nightpeak is a portfolio investment of Energy Spectrum Partners VIII, LP, an infrastructure-focused private equity fund headquartered in Dallas, Texas. - 1. artigo.texto: Proposed 1-year moratorium on data centers, task force fails after Fort Wayne City Council vote FORT WAYNE, Ind. (WPTA) - Proposals for a one-year data center moratorium and a data center task force failed Tuesday, ending a contentious debate between Fort Wayne City Council members. BACKGROUND: Fort Wayne council member proposes one-year data center moratorium Councilwoman Rohli Booker introduced the proposals last month, which would have kept the city council from approving any new data center projects and created a comprehensive data center development standard. It would have stopped short of halting the existing Google data center project underway in southeast Fort Wayne. “If there was ever a perfect time to pause, it’s now,” Booker said ahead of the proposals failing in a 3-to-5 vote for the task force and a 4-to-4 vote for the moratorium. “We know that Fort Wayne has a lot to offer; we have water, we have infrastructure, we have economic development incentives, we have a state that has made it very clear that it wants these types of developments,” she said. “Indiana has practically put up a neon sign saying that ‘We are open for business.’” “I don’t think anyone is confused about that.” Councilman Russ Jehl also voted yes. He said he thinks a big reason why the resolutions weren’t passed is that the Department of Planning Services is now increasing its involvement. “The Department of Planning Services, whose job is to create some guardrails for land use, is finally getting a little bit in motion,” he said. Tonight’s meeting also had a big turnout from a local electrical workers’ union. Recently, members of the union posted on Facebook to express concerns about the moratorium’s potential impact on future jobs. “I think we finally saw some of the stakeholders, like the trades, come and say, ‘Oh, by the way, there are actually some tangible benefits, like my job being produced, and that there are a lot more jobs than the perception is,’” Jehl said. Councilwoman Michelle Chambers was one of the people voting no. She said some definitions in the moratorium were not specific, including the phrase “data centers.” “We cannot have such an open-ended definition,” she said. “We had to be very clear, so that we don’t have other data-driven organizations, corporations, be affected by a moratorium that was attempting to deal with what data centers do.” RELATED: Fort Wayne neighbors say Google data center noise, lights disrupt their lives | Story continues below previous coverage Councilman Nathan Hartman, who has consistently stated his opposition to the proposal, expressed concerns that it would create issues for developments such as schools and hospitals. “I’m still a no on this. I’m not convinced that this is good policy, and I feel like that this sends the wrong message to not just our community, but to our other partners throughout the state,” he said. artigo.texto: Romania’s mergers and acquisitions (M&A) market recorded 212 transactions in the first nine months of 2026, down slightly from 215 deals in the same period last year, according to an analysis by EY. Despite the 1% decline in transaction volume, the estimated value of the market increased by 33% to USD 7.1 billion, from USD 5.4 billion in the first nine months of 2025. The value of disclosed transactions rose by 39% to USD 4.1 billion, driven largely by three major acquisitions announced in the first half of the year. The three largest transactions were Paval Holding’s USD 977 million acquisition of Carrefour Romania, Premier Energy’s USD 824 million acquisition of Evryo Group, and Raiffeisen Bank International’s USD 681 million acquisition of Garanti BBVA Romania. Together, they accounted for approximately 60% of the total disclosed deal value during the period. M&A activity slows in the third quarter Romania’s performance followed a broader international trend of higher transaction values despite declining deal volumes. Across Europe, M&A value increased by 54% in the first nine months of 2026, while global deal value rose by 28%. Meanwhile, transaction volumes fell by 11% in Europe and 8% globally. Following a particularly strong first half, global M&A activity slowed in the third quarter, with total deal value falling below USD 1 trillion for the first time since Q2 2025, according to LSEG. Only ten transactions exceeding USD 10 billion were announced worldwide, the lowest quarterly number of mega-deals since Q4 2024. The slowdown came amid rising energy costs, renewed inflationary pressures, and higher expectations for long-term interest rates. Romania also recorded weaker M&A activity in Q3 2026, with transaction volume down 9% and disclosed deal value falling 15% compared with the same quarter in 2025. No transactions exceeding USD 100 million were announced during the quarter. One notable deal was the acquisition of Pall-Ex Romania by BoldMind Capital Partners and the company’s executive management team through a leveraged buyout valued at approximately USD 29 million. Pall-Ex Romania provides domestic and international palletised freight distribution services as part of a wider European network. Another significant regional development, although outside the scope of EY’s Romanian M&A database, was Canadian group Alimentation Couche-Tard’s announced voluntary tender offer for Żabka Group, Poland’s largest convenience retailer. Żabka operates more than 13,000 stores across Poland and Romania, including the Froo convenience store chain on the Romanian market. The offer implied an equity valuation of approximately USD 8.6 billion. Foreign investors drive deal activity Strategic investors remained the dominant buyers in Romania’s M&A market, accounting for 83% of transaction volume during the first nine months of 2026. Direct acquisitions by financial sponsors declined by 17% year-on-year, with more than one-third involving transactions across multiple countries. However, when acquisitions by private equity-backed companies are also considered, financial sponsor-backed buyers accounted for approximately 28% of total deal volume. Cross-border investment continued to play a significant role. Inbound acquisitions increased by 13% year-on-year to 124 transactions, while domestic deals declined by 10% to 78. Inbound acquisitions also exceeded the 70 transactions involving disposals by foreign-owned businesses, indicating that foreign investors continued to expand their presence in the Romanian market. The United States remained the leading source of foreign investors, with 16 transactions, followed by France and Austria with 11 each. The United Kingdom ranked fourth with seven deals, while Poland followed with six. Real estate and technology lead by deal volume, while energy storage attracts investment Real Estate, Hospitality & Construction remained the most active sector, with 46 transactions during the first nine months of 2026. Technology, Media & Telecommunications (TMT) ranked second with 40 deals, maintaining its position from the corresponding period of 2025. Nearly a quarter of TMT transactions involved technology acquisitions spanning multiple countries, while the telecommunications segment accounted for just one deal. Advanced Manufacturing & Mobility followed with 37 transactions, up 37% year-on-year. The increase was driven entirely by stronger activity in advanced manufacturing, as mobility deal volumes remained unchanged. Foreign buyers accounted for approximately two-thirds of the sector’s transactions. Energy & Utilities ranked fourth with 30 deals, approximately half of which involved foreign acquisitions of battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, reflecting investor interest in Romania’s developing energy storage market. Consumer Products & Retail and Health & Life Sciences each recorded 19 transactions, representing annual declines of 32% and 41%, respectively. The decrease in healthcare-related M&A followed an active period in 2025, when the market recorded a high number of veterinary clinic acquisitions.

artigo.texto: Navitas, NVIDIA collaborate on power delivery board for AI data centers Navitas Semiconductor NVTS announced Monday its latest 24 kW, 800 V-to-12 V DC-DC power delivery board, or PDB. The company highlighted that its power delivery board is powered by GaNFast™ technology and developed in collaboration with NVIDIA NVDA to support the NVIDIA MGX ecosystem and advance 800 VDC power architectures for AI data centers. Shares of NVTS jumped more than 5% in extended trading. This latest 24 kW, 800 V-to-12 V PDB extends Navitas’ portfolio of 800 VDC AI data-center platforms, building on the previously announced 20 kW, 800 V-to-6 V PDB developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, the company noted, adding that "These solutions advance the core strategic focus of the Navitas 2.0 transformation to accelerate the replacement of legacy silicon with next-generation GaN and SiC high-power technologies across AI infrastructure, from Grid-to-xPU." The company highlighted that its power delivery board is designed in NVIDIA’s latest 400 mm × 60 mm form factor and could be integrated onto the compute motherboard as close as possible to the xPUs, minimizing power-delivery losses and supporting high-power demands. “The next era of AI will be defined not only by how much compute we can create but by our ability to deliver the power needed to unleash its full potential,” said Chris Allexandre, President and CEO of Navitas. “Our collaboration with NVIDIA is breaking the AI infrastructure power wall by reimagining power delivery from 800 VDC to the GPU. This next-generation 24 kW solution demonstrates how GaNFast™ technology can eliminate power-conversion stages, increase efficiency and power density, and bring power closer to the GPU.” The company announced that the 800 V-to-12 V PDB is planned to be showcased at the NVIDIA AI Factory MGX Wall partner display area at OCP Global Summit 2026. artigo.texto: Amwins Global Risks (AGR) is expanding its specialist commercial and industrial (C&I) insurance facility to cover battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. The facility groups distributed assets under a single program, with deductibles scaled to individual site characteristics rather than to utility-scale norms. The structure is designed for portfolios that sit between the two ends of the existing insurance market: too small for utility-scale terms, too numerous to place site by site. The London-based wholesale broker has previously applied the same portfolio aggregation logic to distributed solar assets, grouping commercial and community-scale projects under a single program structure. The BESS and EV charging expansion applies that same structure to two asset classes where the market gap is arguably sharper. The BESS insurance market has been expanding, but unevenly. A number of insurers have restricted or withdrawn capacity following battery fires in the UK and overseas, a trend documented by market participants including Allianz UK, which expanded its own BESS underwriting capability in July 2026 partly in response to gaps left by capacity withdrawals. That means brokers face a market where appetite and expertise are not evenly distributed. Allianz UK expanded its own BESS underwriting capability in July 2026, with its head of construction, engineering and energy insurance noting that early engagement with experienced underwriters is increasingly valuable given how quickly the risk landscape is developing. For C&I assets specifically, the challenge is structural as much as technical. Individual sites can be relatively small in value, but developers are assembling portfolios of dozens of them across multiple locations. Applying terms designed for a large utility-scale installation to a single C&I site can produce deductibles that are disproportionate to the asset’s value, making the insurance economically unworkable. The Amwins facility is designed to resolve that by underwriting at portfolio level while still assessing accumulated natural catastrophe exposure across individual locations. “Individual sites can be relatively small, but developers are increasingly building portfolios comprising numerous assets across multiple locations," said Tom Harries, director at Amwins Global Risks. "Bringing those assets together allows us to underwrite them efficiently at portfolio scale, while still recognising the individual risk characteristics of each site.” The facility covers both construction and operational phases, including delay in start-up and business interruption cover. The EV charging component is primarily directed at the US market, where commercial charging infrastructure is being deployed at scale. Amwins Global Risks operates from London and places through the London market, giving US-based developers and their brokers access to London capacity for risks that the domestic US market has been slower to accommodate in structured form. Harries said the addition of BESS and EV charging reflects the increasing convergence of distributed energy technologies, and that the facility is designed to adapt as portfolios grow. “It allows us to focus on monitoring how the portfolio’s natural catastrophe exposure changes as new projects are added and gives developers the freedom to concentrate on building out their portfolios, knowing their insurance program can adapt and grow alongside them.” The C&I expansion follows AGR’s renewal and enlargement of a separate natural catastrophe facility for renewable energy projects in July 2026, which increased available capacity to $50 million per placement from $20 million and broadened cover to all major natural catastrophe perils globally. The two moves extend AGR’s distributed and renewable energy proposition across construction, operation and catastrophe layers within a matter of months.
