The global Battery Manufacturing Machines Market is a critical capital equipment segment enabling the scale-up of battery production for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. This market encompasses machinery for electrode manufacturing, cell assembly, module and pack assembly, and testing. Demand is structurally driven by the proliferation of gigafactories worldwide, supported by regional localization mandates and subsidies. The transition toward advanced chemistries such as LFP, high-nickel NMC, and solid-state batteries is a primary catalyst for capital expenditure, requiring significant retooling and creating opportunities for technology disruptors. The supply chain faces constraints from long lead times for high-precision components, impacting turnkey line delivery. Competitive advantage is bifurcating between integrated turnkey line exporters and specialized process machine leaders. Factory economics increasingly prioritize throughput, yield, and sustainability, driving adoption of dry electrode coating, solvent-free mixing, and AI-powered inspection. The qualification and integration burden elevates the role of system integrators and EPC specialists. After-sales service and spare parts logistics constitute a high-margin segment. Regulatory evolution around battery passports and carbon footprint tracking is becoming a direct design input for manufacturing equipment. The market is forecast to grow at a robust CAGR through 2035, with Asia-Pacific leading in supply and demand, followed by North America and Europe. The baseline scenario for the Battery Manufacturing Machines Market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates robust growth, driven by the global energy transition and the accelerating adoption of electric vehicles. The market is projected to expand at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.2%, reaching a market index of 245 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is underpinned by the continued announcement and construction of gigafactories, particularly in North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia, as governments and automakers invest heavily in localizing battery supply chains. Competitive dynamics are evolving, with turnkey line providers competing on scale and project delivery, while specialized machine makers focus on technological differentiation. The aftermarket for service, upgrades, and spare parts is expected to grow in importance, offering high-margin opportunities. Regionally, Asia-Pacific will maintain its dominance in both production and consumption, but North America and Europe are expected to gain share as localization efforts intensify. Risks to the outlook include potential delays in gigafactory projects, raw material price volatility, and geopolitical tensions affecting supply chains. However, the long-term trajectory remains positive, supported by decarbonization goals and technological advancements. This segment is driven by the rapid expansion of EV production capacity worldwide, as automakers race to electrify their fleets. Battery manufacturing machines are essential for producing lithium-ion cells and packs at scale, with processes including electrode coating, cell assembly, and module/pack assembly. The demand is characterized by high-volume, high-precision requirements, as EV batteries must meet stringent safety, performance, and cost targets. The transition from NMC to LFP chemistries for entry-level EVs will require different equipment, while solid-state batteries may disrupt the market later in the forecast period. Demand-side indicators include EV sales penetration rates, battery pack prices, and government EV mandates. The segment is dominated by major battery manufacturers such as CATL, LG Energy Solution, and Tesla, who are also key customers for machine suppliers. The trend toward vertical integration among automakers and battery makers is expected to influence equipment procurement strategies, with a growing emphasis on turnkey lines and local sourcing. artigo.texto: Land & Expand: North America's Data Center Pipeline Expands Under Pressure Key Highlights - Large-scale projects like Fluidstack's 1.5 GW AI data center in Texas exemplify the industry's move toward industrial-scale infrastructure supporting advanced computing needs. - Community opposition and regulatory scrutiny are increasingly influencing project approvals, as seen in Mahomet, Illinois, where public opposition halted negotiations. - Developers are securing land, power, and water infrastructure while addressing local concerns about environmental impact, noise, and costs, reflecting a more complex development environment. - Major tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and AWS are expanding their regional footprints with multi-phase campuses, often integrating renewable energy and onsite generation. - The data center pipeline remains robust, with projects at various stages—from land acquisition to construction—highlighting ongoing industry growth despite rising development challenges. Land & Expand is Data Center Frontier's periodic look at the latest data center development news, including new sites, land acquisitions and campus expansions across North America. This latest installment finds the development pipeline continuing to expand, even as the requirements for bringing large-scale projects online grow more complicated. Developers are securing land, planning new power infrastructure and advancing campuses measured in hundreds of megawatts or more. At the same time, local governments and residents are demanding greater clarity on electricity costs, water consumption, noise, tax incentives and the long-term effects of industrial-scale computing facilities. A succession of development disclosures and project milestones through September and early October 2026 illustrates both the geographical reach of North America's expanding data center pipeline and the growing difficulty of measuring how much proposed capacity will ultimately be delivered. The projects range from preliminary discussions and newly secured development sites to campuses already under construction. Some are advancing through formal permitting and power studies; others remain contingent on customers, financing or local approvals. Together, they reveal an industry still expanding aggressively, but operating under increasingly complex development conditions. Fluidstack: Cameron County, Texas — Up to 1.5 GW One of the largest newly disclosed projects is Fluidstack's AI data center development in Cameron County in the Rio Grande Valley. The project surfaced publicly September 10 when Cameron County announced that it had issued Fluidstack a worksite permit for property near Harlingen. The permit authorizes preliminary site work, including grading, utilities and related infrastructure, rather than construction of the data center buildings themselves. Fluidstack subsequently disclosed considerably more detail on September 21, saying construction had begun on a $4 billion first phase capable of supporting as much as 1.5 GW. Fluidstack expects the project to generate more than 2,500 construction jobs and several hundred permanent positions. The company has placed unusual emphasis on the project's local infrastructure impact. It says it requested no local property-tax abatements and intends to pay for the energy, water and infrastructure necessary to serve the campus. Cooling will use a recirculating closed-loop system. At up to 1.5 GW in its announced first phase, Cameron County represents a major addition to the Texas AI development pipeline, reflecting the increasingly industrial scale of projects designed to support advanced computing. Microsoft ATL50: Union City, Georgia A new filing for Microsoft's ATL50 campus entered Georgia's Development of Regional Impact review process on September 15. Microsoft filed plans for ATL50, a new data center campus at 5235 Stonewall Tell Road in Union City, southwest of Atlanta. Plans call for two three-story data center buildings totaling approximately 910,000 square feet on 88 acres. The filing projects completion in 2032. Microsoft already has a substantial Georgia footprint, with development activity in Fairburn, Douglasville, Palmetto, Rome, East Point and other communities. ATL50 represents another proposed campus in the greater Atlanta market rather than entry into a new region. No electrical capacity has been disclosed. Project Gravel: Pima County, Arizona Another proposed development emerged through public-records reporting rather than a corporate announcement. Documents obtained in September disclosed Project Gravel, an eight-building data center campus being evaluated on approximately 160 acres of vacant land in unincorporated Pima County west of Sahuarita, Arizona. Plans show eight buildings of roughly 203,000 square feet each, producing a potential campus of approximately 1.6 million square feet, along with a dedicated electrical substation, roads and parking infrastructure. Project documents contemplate full buildout by 2029, contingent on the development advancing through the necessary approvals. County staff had reportedly been evaluating the proposal for months before details became public. Neither the developer nor a prospective tenant has been publicly identified, and the planned electrical load remains undisclosed. The disclosure has already generated local concern: Residents gathered September 29 to discuss the project's potential effects on water, energy use and the surrounding environment. Sahuarita officials subsequently clarified that the proposed site lies outside town boundaries, under Pima County jurisdiction. Project Gravel also illustrates the difficulty in determining the true size of the U.S. development pipeline. Large sites can remain in engineering, environmental and land-use review for months before appearing in conventional industry announcements. artigo.texto: Youdera chega aos 2.500 projetos solares e reforça aposta no armazenamento de energia - A Youdera celebra 11 anos, com mais de 2.500 projetos de energia solar em Portugal, Espanha e Suíça. Apostas em produção local e gestão de energia, são prioridades. - Cinco anos após iniciar operações em Portugal, a empresa foca em soluções de energia descentralizada, integrando armazenamento e inteligência artificial para otimização. - A Youdera pretende instalar 500 megawatts até 2030, especialmente no setor empresarial, através do modelo Energy-as-a-Service, sem investimento inicial dos clientes. Conteúdo Este resumo foi criado com recurso a inteligência artificial. Embora esta tecnologia tenha sido concebida para ser útil e precisa, pode conter erros ou não captar todas as nuances importantes do artigo. Feedback Se consideras que o resumo não está claro ou não reflete bem o conteúdo, envia o teu feedback. A tua opinião é importante para ajudar a melhorar esta funcionalidade! Partilhar Empresa, que opera em Portugal, Espanha e Suíça, pretende atingir 500 MW de potência instalada nos três mercados até 2030. A Youdera assinala 11 anos de atividade com mais de 2.500 projetos de energia solar realizados em Portugal, Espanha e Suíça e pretende reforçar a aposta em sistemas locais que combinam produção fotovoltaica, armazenamento em baterias e gestão de energia, foi divulgado em comunicado. Segundo a mesma fonte, cinco anos depois de iniciar operações em Portugal, a empresa está a direcionar a sua atividade para soluções de energia descentralizada instaladas nas próprias instalações dos clientes, do lado do consumo, o chamado modelo behind the meter. A estratégia passa por combinar a produção solar com baterias e ferramentas digitais de gestão de energia. Segundo a empresa, a plataforma tecnológica, que recorre a inteligência artificial, permite otimizar a utilização da energia produzida localmente e a eletricidade adquirida à rede. A evolução do modelo de negócio acompanha também um reforço da capacidade de investimento. No início de 2026, a Youdera fechou uma ronda estratégica com a Amundi Energy Transition, associada a um plano de implementação de 150 milhões de euros para infraestruturas de energia distribuída. O financiamento deverá ser aplicado na instalação de novos sistemas, na incorporação de armazenamento em ativos existentes e na aquisição de projetos e portefólios já em operação nos três mercados onde a empresa está presente. “O quinto aniversário de operação da Youdera em Portugal é uma ocasião especial. Temos muito orgulho no trabalho que temos feito no país até aqui”, afirma Pedro Miranda, cofundador e CEO da Youdera. A empresa, acrescenta, começou por financiar projetos solares e evoluiu para um modelo em que constrói e opera sistemas locais de energia nas instalações dos clientes, combinando produção, armazenamento e gestão. A Youdera estabeleceu como objetivo alcançar 500 megawatts (MW) de potência instalada em Portugal, Espanha e Suíça até 2030, através da construção de novos sistemas de geração e armazenamento e da aquisição de projetos e portefólios em funcionamento. Em Portugal, a empresa mantém o foco no desenvolvimento de sistemas locais de energia destinados sobretudo ao setor empresarial, num contexto de procura por soluções que permitam reduzir custos energéticos e aumentar a previsibilidade do consumo. O modelo Energy-as-a-Service adotado pela empresa prevê que os clientes não tenham de realizar o investimento inicial nos equipamentos, ficando a Youdera responsável pelo financiamento, instalação e operação dos sistemas.

artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 14 de outubro de 2026, às 15:16 A Cemig anunciou o lançamento de uma chamada pública de projetos de eficiência energética, voltada para atrair iniciativas de clientes da companhia que possibilitem a modernização de unidades consumidoras e propiciem a redução do desperdício ou a geração sustentável de energia elétrica. Foram disponibilizados neste ano cerca de R$ 150 milhões para apoiar as ações, divididos em sete tipologias: Industrial (R$ 40 milhões), Residencial – condomínios (R$ 35 milhões), Comércio e Serviços (R$ 25 milhões), Poder Público (R$ 15 milhões), Serviços Públicos (R$ 15 milhões), Rural (R$ 10 milhões) e Iluminação Pública (R$ 10 milhões). Cada proposta deve contemplar uma única tipologia e prever recursos do Programa de Eficiência Energética (PEE) entre R$ 300 mil e R$ 9 milhões. Segundo a Cemig, a novidade da edição de 2026 da chamada pública é a possibilidade de incluir sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias. Também são elegíveis ações de substituição de equipamentos por modelos mais eficientes em diversos usos finais, como iluminação, condicionamento ambiental, motores e refrigeração, além da instalação de geração por fontes incentivadas, como usinas solares fotovoltaicas. O prazo para submissão das propostas segue até 6 de novembro. Regras A chamada pública integra o Programa de Eficiência Energética da Cemig, regulado pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). Com os projetos aprovados, a Cemig reembolsa as etapas executadas pelo proponente. Para entidades públicas e filantrópicas, o financiamento é feito a fundo perdido. Já as unidades consumidoras de natureza privada e sem fins assistenciais, como indústrias, comércios e condomínios, firmam contrato de desempenho, em que parte do valor retorna à Cemig em até cinco anos, pago com a própria economia de energia gerada pelo projeto. Em 12 anos de chamadas públicas, a Cemig aprovou 177 propostas de clientes, com investimentos de cerca de R$ 171 milhões. Desse total, 114 projetos já foram concluídos. Veja também

artigo.texto: O primeiro sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias integrado a uma usina solar no Brasil iniciou os testes em Salvador, Bahia, sob autorização da Aneel. A iniciativa, realizada na usina Sol de Brotas 7 da Statkraft, permite guardar o sol do dia para usar à noite, aumentando a eficiência e valor dos ativos renováveis. Salvador, outubro de 2026. O início dos testes do primeiro sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) integrado a uma usina solar no Brasil representa um marco para a evolução do setor elétrico nacional. Instalado na usina solar Sol de Brotas 7, da Statkraft, na Bahia, o projeto combina geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento de energia, abrindo caminho para novos modelos de operação, maior flexibilidade da rede e uma gestão mais eficiente dos ativos renováveis. Para a Voltxs Energia, o avanço demonstra que o armazenamento deixa de ser apenas uma tecnologia promissora e passa a integrar as estratégias de desenvolvimento dos empreendimentos renováveis. À medida que a participação das fontes solar e eólica cresce na matriz elétrica brasileira, aumenta também a necessidade de soluções capazes de conferir maior previsibilidade, flexibilidade e eficiência à operação desses ativos. - Primeiro sistema de baterias (BESS) integrado a usina solar no Brasil inicia testes. - Projeto autorizado pela Aneel está localizado na usina Sol de Brotas 7, na Bahia. - Tecnologia permite armazenar energia gerada durante o dia para uso posterior. - A integração busca aumentar a flexibilidade e eficiência da rede elétrica nacional. - A Voltxs Energia destaca que a gestão inteligente dos ativos ganha novo status estratégico. Matheus Ivanoski Teixeira, Diretor de Operações (COO) da Voltxs Energia, afirma que o início do projeto representa um passo importante para a maturidade do mercado brasileiro de armazenamento de energia. Ele destaca que o BESS deixa de ser apenas um tema de planejamento e passa a ser validado na prática como um componente estratégico. A combinação entre geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento amplia as possibilidades de gestão da energia produzida e prepara o setor para uma matriz cada vez mais dinâmica. Armazenamento passa a integrar a estratégia dos ativos Os sistemas BESS permitem armazenar a energia gerada em momentos de maior produção e disponibilizá-la quando houver necessidade operacional ou maior demanda do sistema elétrico. Na avaliação da Voltxs, o principal ganho está na integração entre geração, armazenamento e gestão inteligente dos ativos. Teixeira explica que, ao analisar um projeto híbrido, não se fala apenas da instalação de baterias. O grande diferencial está na capacidade de integrar geração, armazenamento e inteligência operacional para extrair mais eficiência dos ativos. Essa visão tende a se tornar cada vez mais relevante para investidores, operadores e proprietários de usinas. Segundo o executivo, os primeiros projetos em operação terão papel fundamental para fornecer dados reais sobre desempenho, dimensionamento, custos, retorno econômico e aplicações do armazenamento em diferentes cenários. Mercado entra em uma nova fase O avanço também reforça uma tendência observada internacionalmente: a evolução das usinas renováveis para plataformas energéticas mais inteligentes. Essas plataformas são capazes de combinar diferentes tecnologias e responder de forma mais eficiente às necessidades do sistema elétrico. Na avaliação da Voltxs, essa transformação deve impulsionar novos modelos de negócios, ampliar a competitividade dos empreendimentos renováveis e acelerar investimentos em soluções de armazenamento nos próximos anos. Teixeira destaca que os projetos pioneiros serão importantes para definir as melhores estratégias de utilização do armazenamento no Brasil. O aprendizado obtido nessa fase permitirá desenvolver modelos mais eficientes tanto do ponto de vista operacional quanto econômico. A tendência é que a gestão integrada dos ativos passe a ser um diferencial competitivo para o setor. Além dos benefícios operacionais, a integração entre geração fotovoltaica e armazenamento fortalece a discussão sobre a modernização da infraestrutura elétrica brasileira, criando condições para uma matriz energética mais flexível, resiliente e preparada para a expansão das fontes renováveis.

artigo.texto: Desenvolve SP e Möbius criam FIDC de R$ 70 milhões para financiar data centers Fundo terá como foco provedores regionais de internet e operadores de data centers de pequeno porte, especialmente em cidades do interior com menor oferta de conectividade e serviços tecnológicos A Desenvolve SP e a gestora Möbius Capital estão lançando um fundo de investimento em direitos creditórios (FIDC) de R$ 70 milhões para financiar empresas de infraestrutura digital no Estado de São Paulo. O fundo terá como foco provedores regionais de internet e operadores de data centers de pequeno porte, especialmente em cidades do interior com menor oferta de conectividade e serviços tecnológicos. A agência de fomento paulista subscreverá R$ 50 milhões em cotas seniores, equivalentes a 71,4% do patrimônio previsto para o FIDC, enquanto a Möbius ficará com R$ 20 milhões em cotas subordinadas, ou 28,6% do total. Na estrutura, as cotas subordinadas absorvem primeiro eventuais perdas da carteira, funcionando como uma camada de proteção para as cotas seniores, que têm prioridade no recebimento de amortizações e rendimentos, conforme as regras do fundo. Assim, a gestora assume a primeira parcela do risco de crédito das operações, enquanto a Desenvolve SP ocupa a posição prioritária na distribuição dos recursos. O fundo poderá antecipar recebíveis de clientes dos provedores de internet, tanto pessoas físicas quanto jurídicas, além de financiar a aquisição de equipamentos e projetos de expansão da infraestrutura tecnológica. Também estão previstas operações relacionadas à compra e à fusão de empresas, em um mercado que passa por um processo de consolidação. A Möbius foi selecionada em chamada pública da Desenvolve SP voltada a FIDCs e fundos de investimento em participações (FIPs). Segundo Roberto Savaris, sócio e fundador da gestora, a casa já atua no financiamento de aquisições de provedores de internet e na estruturação de operações no mercado de capitais para empresas do setor. A proposta passou por análise de elegibilidade, diligência e aprovação pelo comitê de investimentos da agência de fomento. Para Ricardo Brito, diretor-presidente da Desenvolve SP, a operação busca ampliar o acesso ao crédito para negócios inovadores por meio da combinação de capital público e privado. “Por meio do ‘blended finance’, conseguimos atrair investimento privado, potencializar o impacto do recurso público e alcançar mais empreendedores”, afirmou.

artigo.texto: Phoenix is stationing inspectors at Menlo Digital’s Ahwatukee data center construction site in the early morning and has secured a series of commitments from the contractor to reduce noise and other disturbances following complaints from nearby residents. The measures include moving construction traffic farther from homes, restricting early-morning deliveries, relocating employee parking and monitoring noise levels around the property. In an Oct. 9 email to residents, Mike Baxley, assistant director of the city's Planning and Development Department, said the city met with the construction management team and a representative of the project's ownership to address neighborhood concerns. “As with all construction projects, there is a certain amount of noise that the activity of construction will create,” he wrote. “The contractor has committed to taking steps to minimize these aspects of those types of issues.” Baxley’s email was the city’s latest reaction to months of complaints by residents about construction noise, bright lighting and work they contend was occurring outside legally permitted hours at the million-square-foot Menlo Digital data center campus near 48th Street and Thistle Landing Drive. "Earlier today we were able to have a meeting with the onsite management team and a representative of ownership for the Thistle Landing project to identify ways to soften the challenges that neighbors are facing with this project," Baxley wrote. His email also came days before two developments are set this week, one involving the Menlo project and the other data centers generally. On Friday, Oct. 16, construction hours return to a wintertime schedule, with crews permitted to work outside only between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. Monday to Friday unless they secure a special permit from the city Planning and Development Department City Planning Director Joshua Bednarik several weeks ago told residents in an email his department will not give the Menlo Digital data campus company such a permit. From 5-6:30 p.m. today, Oct. 14, Attorney General Kris Mayes will hold a town hall on data centers at The Eagles Community Center, 828 E. Broadway Road, Mesa. “The AG is not investigating the Ahwatukee data center approval,” said Richie Taylor, the attorney general’s communications director. “She is holding a townhall to hear directly from residents about their concerns after receiving multiple complaints from the community.” Mayes subsequently broadened the the town hall's scope to data centers generally. The most significant immediate change outlined by Baxley involves city inspectors. "Starting today, I have asked our Inspections team to have after hours inspectors onsite, in the morning, each work day to ensure that no activity takes place prior to legal start times through the end of the state mandated early construction" period, he wrote. "My hope is that this will ensure compliance and allow the neighbors not to have to worry about having to call in a complaint as we will already have an inspector there to handle any infraction of the mandated start times." The decision represents a more direct approach to monitoring construction activity than relying solely on complaints from neighbors. However, Baxley's email does not indicate that the city has determined any violations occurred. He said his staff is investigating complaints filed Sept. 12, 24, 25, 26 and Oct. 2 to establish what happened and whether enforcement action was warranted. "We use a call service that logs the complaints and notifies the on-call inspector that day," Baxley wrote. "Once I get more information on the complaints for these dates I can respond further as to what the determination of the complaints were and if any action was necessary." The latest development comes as the controversial data center project continues to face opposition from nearby residents, who have raised concerns about its potential effects on their neighborhood. Much of the broader dispute has centered on the facility's anticipated operations, including questions about noise, electricity consumption and other environmental and health impacts. Construction itself quickly evolved as a separate source of friction, particularly for residents living closest to the site. Craig Evans, president of the Ahwatukee Community Alliance, a nonprofit opponents formed to fight the facility, was not impressed by Baxley's message. "It didn’t seem to mean much," he said. "As far as the City of Phoenix seems concerned, the citizens that do most of the living, working and dying in Ahwatukee...aren't all that important to the permitting process. "Disruption to the peace and tranquility of our homes seems an acceptable sacrifice to the City of Phoenix once a permit is issued." "Quite frankly Mr. Baxley should be standing in our neighborhood in the small hours making his own recordings and protecting our interests, rather we suspect his are just the latest effort to discount and dismiss the concerns and suffering the City’s decisions have already inflicted on Ahwatukee." Evans then lashed out at the city process that got the neighbors in the position they're now in. Baxley's email outlines several changes the contractor has agreed to make. Through Oct. 15, when early construction hours are scheduled to end, the contractor has committed not to open the project's gates or turn on construction lighting before the legally permitted start time. artigo.texto: Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Apontada como um dos principais entraves para que projetos de reflorestamento e de Redução das Emissões por Desmatamento e Degradação Florestal (Redd+) consigam acessar linhas de financiamento, a modelagem dos contratos passará a ter um padrão, que está em desenvolvimento pelo Nature Investment Lab (NIL). A minuta desse contrato modelo foi apresentada publicamente durante a Semana do Clima que aconteceu recentemente em Nova York e, para elaborá-la, o NIL conversou com 25 importantes instituições. Entre elas, Itaú BBA, Regia Capital, Systemica, Petrobras e Regreen. No próximo passo, o rascunho do contrato modelo será colocado em audiência pública e deve ganhar destaque durante a COP31, que acontecerá entre os dias 9 e 20 de novembro na Turquia. A meta é concluir o trabalho até o final deste ano. O NIL aposta no processo de amadurecimento desse mercado, que já vem durando mais de 20 anos e que deverá elevar o carbono ao status de commodity, com possibilidade de ser negociado internacionalmente. “A ideia é preparar os desenvolvedores dos projetos de produção de carbono para que consigam lidar com todas as exigências com as quais vão se deparar quando tentarem acessar recursos”, explica Fabiana Philipi, gerente de projetos da Climate Ventures, organização que lidera o NIL. Ela pondera, no entanto, que o documento de referência poderá ajudar os outros players desse mercado, como os compradores e financiadores do mercado de carbono. Segundo Philipi, as propostas de produção de carbono bem elaboradas têm forte demanda e o objetivo é ajudar desenvolvedores de todos os portes, desde empresas já consagradas como Re.Green e Mombak, até aquelas que estão dando os primeiros passos. As maiores compradoras dos créditos de carbono brasileiros, atualmente, são as big techs, principalmente a Microsoft. A minuta apresentada em Nova York refere-se a contratos offtake — compra mínima garantida — que são acordos jurídicos firmados entre comprador e vendedor de uma mercadoria, antes dela entrar em produção. O documento apresenta cláusulas referentes à estrutura comercial, como preço, pagamento e financiamento, garantias, recebíveis e financiadores, ciclo de vida dos créditos, entrega e titularidade, falha de entrega, entre outros. O NIL é um laboratório de investimentos criado a partir de uma iniciativa que reúne o Banco do Brasil, o Instituto Itaúsa, o Instituto Clima e Sociedade (iCS), o Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) e a internacional Gfanz. O seu objetivo é atrair e estruturar financiamentos, além de promover inovação financeira, para ampliar a chamada economia de Soluções Baseadas na Natureza (NBS, em inglês). Por Cristina Canas

artigo.texto: Data center é desativado temporariamente na Rússia após ataques de drones da Ucrânia Drones ucranianos atingiram instalações da empresa de tecnologia russa Yandex A empresa russa de tecnologia e inteligência artificial Yandex informou que sua infraestrutura foi danificada em um ataque de drones, provocando a paralisação completa de seu data center na região de Vladimir, na região central da Rússia. Ninguém ficou ferido no ataque, mas alguns serviços da Yandex estão indisponíveis para os usuários desde domingo, informou a empresa. Em nota, a companhia disse estar restabelecendo gradualmente a prestação de serviços. Este é o terceiro grande data center a ser tirado de operação nos últimos dias. Na sexta-feira, a Yandex, que tem forte atuação no desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial na Rússia e às vezes é chamada de "Google russo", informou que seu data center na região de Kaluga, a sudoeste de Moscou, havia sido atingido por drones ucranianos e ficado parcialmente fora de operação. Um dia antes, um ataque ucraniano havia provocado a paralisação do data center da Yandex em Sasovo, a sudeste de Moscou, onde estão instalados dois dos três supercomputadores utilizados para desenvolver o modelo de inteligência artificial da empresa.

artigo.texto: Global energy storage targets for 2030 have nearly tripled since the adoption of the COP29 Global Energy Storage and Grids Pledge, reaching 822 GW. However, the combined national commitments remain approximately 45% below the 1,500 GW target established under the international agreement, according to a new analysis by energy think tank Ember. The report highlights a significant increase in global energy storage ambitions, with the combined 2030 targets of 99 countries and the European Union rising by 190%, or approximately 2.9 times, compared with levels assessed during COP29. Despite this progress, national commitments remain below both the global pledge and BloombergNEF’s market forecast, which projects approximately 1,200 GW of battery storage deployment alone by 2030. According to Ember, the increase in storage targets has been driven predominantly by China and the European Union, while most other countries have maintained their existing commitments or have yet to establish dedicated energy storage targets. China has emerged as the largest contributor to the increase in global storage ambitions. Under its 15th Five-Year Plan, the country raised its 2030 energy storage target by 330 GW, from 130 GW to 460 GW. The revised target covers new-type energy storage technologies, primarily batteries, alongside pumped hydro storage. Meanwhile, the European Union established its first bloc-wide energy storage target in June 2026, setting a goal of 200 GW by 2030. Together, China and the EU now account for more than 80% of the combined national storage targets worldwide. Dr Katye Altieri, Global Program Consultant at Ember, noted that the increase in global storage ambition has been concentrated in these two major economies. She emphasised that several leading solar markets have yet to establish storage targets, potentially limiting investment certainty and long-term market development. The analysis also indicates that actual energy storage deployment is advancing considerably faster than national policy commitments. Annual battery storage additions have increased by nearly 80% per year since 2020, significantly exceeding the growth rate required to achieve the COP29 pledge. Global energy storage installations reached a record 118 GW in 2025. Ember estimates that maintaining this annual deployment rate through 2030 would be sufficient to meet the current combined national targets, highlighting the gap between market activity and government policy ambitions. The report further identifies a strong relationship between solar power expansion and energy storage commitments. Countries with ambitious solar capacity targets generally demonstrate stronger energy storage ambitions, although several major solar markets remain exceptions. Among the world’s 20 largest solar markets, eight countries have not established specific energy storage targets for 2030. These include the United States, Germany, and Saudi Arabia, despite their ongoing investments in large-scale battery storage infrastructure. The United States has already installed approximately 52 GW of utility-scale battery storage capacity, while Saudi Arabia has recently connected what Ember describes as the world’s largest single battery storage project. However, other markets, including Poland, Austria, Switzerland, and Brazil, continue to lag in both storage target-setting and deployment. Ember emphasised that rapid market growth does not eliminate the importance of national storage targets. While battery storage projects are progressing in several major economies, deployment remains concentrated in a limited number of markets. Clear national targets can help address regulatory barriers, improve investment confidence, support grid planning, and strengthen coordination between renewable energy development and energy storage infrastructure. The analysis also connects the importance of storage expansion with upcoming international electrification commitments. Ahead of COP31, Türkiye’s presidency is promoting the proposed 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge, which aims to increase electricity’s share of final energy demand from approximately 20% to 35% by 2035. According to Ember, achieving these electrification objectives will require substantial investment in renewable electricity generation, modernised transmission and distribution networks, and sufficient energy storage capacity to manage rising electricity demand. The findings underscore the growing importance of battery energy storage systems and other flexibility technologies in supporting global renewable energy integration, improving electricity grid reliability, and accelerating the transition toward low-carbon energy systems. While energy storage deployment continues to accelerate worldwide, Ember’s assessment indicates that stronger and more geographically diversified national commitments will be necessary to align government policies with the COP29 target of 1,500 GW by 2030. artigo.texto: Marrakech – Gotion Power Morocco (GPM) will begin commissioning and starting up the production equipment at its battery gigafactory in Kenitra during the week of October 20. The subsidiary of Chinese group Gotion High-Tech announced the schedule in a statement, describing the plant as the first of its kind in Africa and the Middle East. The startup opens the way to industrial production of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, built from lithium, iron, and phosphate, within a first phase of 20 GWh. GPM president Khalid Qalam had earlier revealed that the first cell line would begin in October, with a second line following in November. He also pointed to a start of sales for assembled batteries by the end of the year. The site sits inside the Atlantic Free Zone of Kenitra and drew MAD 13 billion ($1.3 billion) in investment for its first phase. It will produce cells and batteries for the automotive and energy storage sectors, serving the Moroccan market and the African continent, along with Europe, the Middle East, and the United States. Construction began in September 2025 after earthworks, and the buildings and infrastructure of the cell plant were completed in 13 months. According to GPM, that timeline ranks the project among the fastest industrial builds of its kind internationally. The work relied on a logistics operation of a scale new to Moroccan industry, with several thousand containers shipped from China to move production lines and high-technology equipment to Kenitra, backed by port and customs authorities. “The startup of the equipment on October 20 is only a first step in the rollout of a unique and promising project, meant to durably structure Morocco’s battery industrial ecosystem,” Qalam noted. He tied the plant to “the kingdom’s sovereignty in the field of green energy.” GPM has so far recruited more than 400 Moroccan employees, among them engineers, technicians, operators, and support staff. Most trained in China at Gotion High-Tech production sites, then worked alongside group experts in Kenitra. At full development, the gigafactory will create more than 2,300 direct jobs. The first phase targets 20 GWh of cells, battery packs, and energy storage systems, plus 100,000 tons of cathode materials. The project advanced further on September 28, when Volkswagen, a Gotion High-Tech shareholder, joined the Chinese group in announcing a Kenitra joint venture for cathode materials. That venture forms part of a broader Gotion-Volkswagen plan to invest about €3.22 billion ($3.67 billion) across battery and materials projects in Europe and North Africa, split between roughly €1.6 billion from Gotion and €1.62 billion from PowerCo, Volkswagen’s battery unit. The companies plan joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia, and Morocco, with the Kenitra cathode project set at about €480 million and 100,000 metric tons a year, prioritizing supplies to the two European battery plants. Gotion will control the Moroccan venture with a 51% stake, and PowerCo will hold 49%. Financing arrived earlier in the year. On July 24, the African Development Bank (AfDB) approved a €100 million loan to GPM for the integrated LFP gigafactory, with plans to mobilize up to €141 million more from partners. The bank described a first phase of 10 GWh scaling toward 100 GWh, and projected more than 600 direct jobs and a 70% local industrial integration rate. Gotion ranked fifth among global EV battery makers over the first seven months of 2026, with installations of 34.0 GWh, up 44.2% from a year earlier.

artigo.texto: BOSTON, Sept. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Factorial Energy Inc. (“Factorial”) (Nasdaq: FAC), a global leader in solid-state battery technology, today announced a strategic partnership with Mitsui Kinzoku Company, Limited to support the industrialization of its Solstice™ all-solid-state battery platform. Mitsui Kinzoku is a leading producer of sulfide-based solid electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries, one of few companies worldwide with foundational technology in this space, and already the global leader in ultra-thin copper foil, with an estimated 90% share of the semiconductor market for that foil. That materials science expertise underpins its A-SOLiD™ sulfide solid electrolyte, unveiled in 2016 and advancing toward mass production at a dedicated plant in Saitama, Japan. "I am very pleased that we have been able to enter into this joint development agreement with Factorial," said Dr. Kiyotaka Yasuda, Senior Executive Officer, General Manager, Business Creation Division of Mitsui Kinzoku Company, Limited. "Batteries are a key technology for realizing an electrified society, but significant technical challenges still remain. That is precisely why we believe it is necessary to go beyond the extension of existing technologies and take on the challenge of creating new value. By leveraging Mitsui Kinzoku's long-established expertise in materials and manufacturing technologies and combining it with Factorial's advanced technological capabilities, we aim to accelerate the realization of next-generation batteries." Factorial remains the fabless innovator across the platform, leading cell design, process development, supply chain qualification, line integration, and manufacturing validation. “Battery innovation can't be done by one single company," said Siyu Huang, CEO of Factorial. "It's driven by the entire supply chain and, increasingly, by an entire industry coalition. Mitsui Kinzoku's foundational electrolyte technology brings critical materials expertise to our work to move Solstice™ toward commercial deployment. We're not just building a battery. We're building the connective thread that helps the whole industry move forward together.” As robotics, aerospace systems, and AI-enabled infrastructure ask more of the physical world, energy is fast becoming the defining constraint on what's possible. Factorial calls this the emergence of the energy layer - the battery infrastructure needed to power the next era of mobility, aerospace and physical intelligence. Built for that layer, Solstice™, Factorial's sulfide-based all-solid-state battery platform, delivers high energy density and improved thermal stability, with proprietary dry-cathode processing enabling more cost-effective manufacturing. This collaboration builds on Factorial's recent momentum, including strategic investments from IQT and POSCO Future M; its first commercial orders for passenger vehicles in January and for aerospace in July; expanded automotive and industrialization partnership programs; and its June 2026 Nasdaq listing under the ticker symbol FAC. Factorial Energy (Nasdaq: FAC) is a leading American solid-state battery innovator backed by IQT – the not-for-profit strategic investor for the U.S. national security community and America’s allies – and Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, Hyundai, and Kia. Through its proprietary FEST® and Solstice™ platforms, engineered for scalable manufacturing, Factorial delivers industry-leading performance across aerospace, energy storage and mobility applications. In 2026, Factorial's initial drone flight test achieved 30% longer range, and the company secured its first commercial orders in both aerospace and passenger vehicle applications. In automotive, Mercedes-Benz’ real-world road testing in a lightly modified test vehicle achieved over 1,200 km of range on a single charge, with the technology also successfully integrated into a fully built Dodge Charger Daytona demonstration vehicle in partnership with Stellantis.. For more information, visit www.factorialenergy.com. Mitsui Kinzoku is a Japan-based global materials company and a leading manufacturer of non-ferrous metals and advanced materials, providing innovative solutions primarily for the automotive and electronics industries. Leveraging its core strengths in non-ferrous metals, functional materials, and recycling technologies, the company develops and manufactures a wide range of high-performance products, including automotive components, semiconductor materials, battery materials, and engineered materials. With a strong focus on innovation, environmental responsibility, and resource circulation, Mitsui Kinzoku collaborates with partners around the world to create new value and will continue to contribute to the realization of a sustainable society. artigo.texto: News Should Tesla move away from its battery technology? Should Tesla replace its current battery system when it works so well? The cylindrical battery which measures 18 mm wide and 65 mm in height, hence its name 18/650, has been the main component of Tesla’s battery pack, but could there be a possibility that it would soon move away from this proven technology? Tesla isn’t married to 18650 Tesla Chief Technology Officer JB Straubel has recently said the company isn’t married to cylindrical cells and the company would move to flat cell manufacturing if and when there are greater advantages to replacing the 18650. A 2000 study called “Trading is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors” evaluated 66,465 U.S. households that held stocks from 1991 to 1996. The households that traded most averaged an 11.4% annual return during a period where the overall market gained 17.9%. These lower returns were attributed to overconfidence. A 2014 paper (revised 2019) titled “Learning Fast or Slow?” analyzed the complete transaction history of the Taiwan Stock Exchange between 1992 and 2006. It looked at the ongoing performance of day traders in this sample, and found that 97% of day traders can expect to lose money from trading, and more than 90% of all day trading volume can be traced to investors who predictably lose money. Additionally, it tied the behavior of gamblers and drivers who get more speeding tickets to overtrading, and cited studies showing that legalized gambling has an inverse effect on trading volume. A 2019 research study (revised 2020) called “Day Trading for a Living?” observed 19,646 Brazilian futures contract traders who started day trading from 2013 to 2015, and recorded two years of their trading activity. The study authors found that 97% of traders with more than 300 days actively trading lost money, and only 1.1% earned more than the Brazilian minimum wage ($16 USD per day). They hypothesized that the greater returns shown in previous studies did not differentiate between frequent day traders and those who traded rarely, and that more frequent trading activity decreases the chance of profitability. These studies show the wide variance of the available data on day trading profitability. One thing that seems clear from the research is that most day traders lose money . ExxonMobil vai priorizar a exploração de petróleo na Guiana, ameaçando planos de exportação de gás
Com a redução da oferta de gás natural, o governo guianense avalia redimensionar para baixo a capacidade da infraestrutura de GNL planejada ou abrir mão totalmente das vendas externas
A ExxonMobil informou ao governo da Guiana que precisará reter volumes maiores de gás natural para maximizar a extração de petróleo do que as autoridades locais previam, reduzindo a oferta disponível para projetos de gás natural liquefeito (GNL) e exportação, segundo duas pessoas próximas às negociações.
Diante do alerta, as autoridades guianenses avaliam redimensionar para baixo a capacidade da infraestrutura de GNL planejada ou abrir mão totalmente das vendas externas, priorizando o uso do insumo para geração termelétrica doméstica e plantas petroquímicas.
A eventual desistência ou redução representaria um revés para a ambição do país sul-americano de se posicionar como um polo exportador de energia na região, em um momento em que segue expandindo sua produção de hidrocarbonetos.
Pressão do governo
O governo da Guiana vinha pressionando o consórcio operado pela Exxon, responsável pela totalidade da produção de petróleo e gás do país, a disponibilizar o máximo possível de gás à costa, buscando acelerar a monetização de reservas que estão entre as maiores da América do Sul.
No entanto, o grupo liderado pela petrolífera americana, que conta também com a Chevron e a chinesa CNOOC, estima que serão necessários cerca de 2 bilhões de pés cúbicos de gás por dia para reinjeção nos reservatórios.
O procedimento é considerado indispensável pela operadora para manter a pressão dos poços e cumprir as metas de extração de petróleo bruto nos projetos já autorizados pelo governo, relataram as fontes.
A retenção desses volumes restringe o fornecimento para qualquer empreendimento voltado à exportação de gás, incluindo a unidade flutuante de GNL (FLNG) proposta pela americana Fulcrum LNG, selecionada pelo governo em 2024 para desenvolver a infraestrutura do setor no país.
Em vez da capacidade inicial projetada de 6 milhões de toneladas por ano, o empreendimento, agora, pode ter de iniciar as operações com até 3 milhões de toneladas anuais, deixando eventuais expansões para etapas posteriores, de acordo com as fontes.
A ExxonMobil vem refinando os estudos técnicos para quantificar o potencial de fornecimento dos campos, bem como os custos e os prazos associados. O ministro de Recursos Naturais da Guiana, Vickram Bharrat, já havia cobrado maior clareza da companhia sobre os volumes disponíveis no início deste ano, mas evitou comentar o andamento das conversas nesta semana.
A indefinição sobre o destino do gás remanescente tem gerado frustração entre potenciais investidores. Segundo interlocutores, a redução do porte do terminal de GNL é o caminho mais provável. No momento, a prioridade da administração do presidente Irfaan Ali é colocar em operação uma usina termelétrica a gás para supr
